section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does an orange-colored road sign generally indicate?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance activities; slow down and be prepared for changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow, vehicles on the side of the broken line may pass when safe; vehicles next to the solid line may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross a dashed white line:
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:At any time.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The exact speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,c:Only a suggested speed to follow.
note: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed for ideal conditions; you should drive slower when road, weather, or traffic conditions demand it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Signal your intent a few seconds before turning.,b:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Increase your speed then turn.
note: Activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before turning to warn other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution through an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the driver behind you signals they want to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down to allow space in front of your vehicle for a safe pass.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Maintain exactly the same speed.
note: Slow slightly to create a gap ahead of your vehicle so the overtaking driver can pass more quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,c:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection if it is clear. You may also turn, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you drive in fog to reduce risk?
options: a:Reduce speed, drive cautiously, and use low-beam headlights.,b:Use high beams to see farther.,c:Use hazard lights only.
note: In fog, slow down, be cautious, and use low beams because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check behind the vehicle on foot before getting in.,b:Check rearview mirrors only.,c:Honk immediately before reversing.
note: Because it's hard to see from the driver's seat, walk to the rear of the vehicle first to check for children or objects before backing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What have studies shown about wearing a seat belt properly?
options: a:It reduces the risk of serious injury in a crash.,b:It increases the chance of fatality.,c:It reduces damage to your vehicle.
note: Properly worn seat belts significantly reduce the chances of serious injury or death in crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, smoking, talking or texting, changing the radio.,b:Only texting.,c:Only adjusting the radio.
note: Many common tasks—eating, phone use, or adjusting audio—distract drivers and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To help prevent fatigue on a long trip, what should you do?
options: a:Do arm exercises every hour.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time.,c:Stop and rest approximately every two hours.
note: To reduce fatigue, stop regularly—about every two hours—for a short break, rest, or stretch; if drowsy, stop driving immediately and rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph take to stop?
options: a:Up to 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.
note: Large, fully loaded tractor-trailers require much longer distances to stop than passenger cars—up to nearly 400 feet at 55 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Regarding pedestrians, what is the driver's responsibility?
options: a:Do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian and yield the right-of-way.,b:Only yield if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Assume pedestrians must yield to vehicles.
note: Drivers must be alert and yield to pedestrians to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is not lawfully crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What factor significantly affects your ability to stop a vehicle?
options: a:Road conditions (wet, icy, gravel),b:Signal lights ahead,c:Time of day only
note: Stopping distance is heavily influenced by road surface and condition; reduce speed accordingly when roads are poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No.,b:Yes.,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing or crossing for either direction except to turn into a driveway or similar approved location.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond when near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way because vehicles have priority.,c:Proceed normally without slowing down.
note: Slow, yield, and be ready to stop whenever you encounter a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog to ensure their safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What effect does alcohol have on reflexes and reaction time?
options: a:Puts you to sleep.,b:Wakes you up.,c:Slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reducing reaction time and impairing judgment and coordination needed for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the safest reaction?
options: a:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,b:Flash your lights to let them know they are wrong.,c:Speed up and try to retaliate.
note: Avoid escalating the situation. Remain calm, give the aggressive driver space, and if necessary report the incident to authorities when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an emergency vehicle stopped on the right with lights flashing, you should:
options: a:Maintain your current speed and move quickly into a lane farther away from the emergency vehicle.,b:Maintain your current speed and drive in the right lane.,c:Reduce your speed and safely vacate the lane closest to the emergency vehicle.
note: Slow down and move over one lane away from stopped emergency vehicles when it is safe to do so; if you cannot safely change lanes, reduce speed and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road with an obstructed view approaching a curve, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop the car, get out, and walk around the curve to see what is there.,b:Rapidly turn your headlights on and off several times.,c:Sound your horn and stay close to the right edge of the road while proceeding carefully.
note: If visibility is blocked on a narrow mountain road, sound your horn to warn oncoming traffic and proceed slowly while staying close to the right edge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement regarding railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.,c:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
note: You must obey flaggers, stop signs, and active warning devices; it is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) and it starts to lose traction, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: If your vehicle has ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will pump the brakes automatically to help you maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do round traffic signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:Railroad crossings ahead.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Circular signs are used for railroad crossing warnings; approach them with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Turn on your car radio.,b:Slow down.,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest, stretch, and refresh; do not rely solely on caffeine or music to prevent drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How early should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.,b:Signal only just before you change lanes.,c:Signal after you begin the lane change.
note: You should signal early enough so other drivers understand your intentions before you start the passing maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: If a train is close enough to be a hazard, you must not cross the tracks until the train has fully passed and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being tailgated and there is an open lane to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Move over to the right lane if it is safe to do so.,b:Slow down abruptly to discourage the tailgater.,c:Increase your speed to put more distance between you.
note: If a lane is available to the right, move over to let the tailgater pass; if not, slow gradually when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a flashing yellow traffic signal, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means caution — slow down and proceed carefully if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What color pavement markings separate lanes moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Yellow and white
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you be prepared to do?
options: a:Move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass only when it is safe and legal.,b:Use the shoulder to pass the vehicle.,c:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic to warn them.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road often requires entering the oncoming lane; only pass when you can do so safely and legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop immediately at the scene.,b:Help the injured if it is safe to do so.,c:Call the police if necessary.
note: Stop at the scene, render aid if you can safely do so, call emergency services and the police, and exchange information; do not leave.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the safest way to transport small children in a vehicle?
options: a:Use proper child restraint seats appropriate for the child's size and age.,b:Have a strong adult hold the child in their arms.,c:Allow the child to stand in the back seat.
note: Children must be secured in appropriate child safety seats or boosters; no adult can safely hold a child during a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What maneuvers are allowed from a center left-turn lane marked for left turns?
options: a:You may make left turns from the lane.,b:You may make U-turns.,c:You may pass slow-moving traffic.
note: A center left-turn lane is reserved for left turns (and for completing U-turns where permitted); it is not for passing or through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out due to a power outage, how should you proceed at an intersection?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield accordingly.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and go through without stopping.,c:Park and wait for power to be restored.
note: When signals are not functioning, drivers should yield in the same order as at a four-way stop and proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which item is NOT a factor in determining how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Steering ability,b:Braking distance,c:Reaction distance
note: Stopping distance is determined by perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a direct factor in stopping distance calculation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What can happen to a bicyclist who does not obey traffic laws?
options: a:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists have the same responsibilities and duties as drivers; they can be cited for violations of traffic laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped by a police officer, how should you behave?
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,b:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,c:Remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
note: Stay in your vehicle unless instructed otherwise, keep your hands visible (on the wheel), and wait for the officer to request your documents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Be alert to motorcycles because:
options: a:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,b:They rarely use their headlights.,c:They are more difficult to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see; they can be hidden in blind spots and their speed/distance are harder to judge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:
options: a:The traffic signal is broken.,b:You do not have to come to a complete stop.,c:The same thing as a stop sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must treat the intersection like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always indicates what?
options: a:A speed limit sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) sign is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a full stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection.

question: What effect does alcohol have on your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.,b:It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.,c:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol reduces your ability to drive safely by slowing reaction time, blurring vision, reducing coordination, and harming judgment, so both driving skills and decision‑making are impaired.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only at the top of hills.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines mean no passing from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when instructed by traffic control or emergency personnel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you turn your wheels when parking downhill on a two-way street?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left (away from curb).,b:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).
note: When parking facing downhill on a two‑way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will hit the curb and help prevent it from rolling into traffic.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches from behind?
options: a:Speed up to create distance between you and the emergency vehicle.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Immediately pull to the curb or edge of the roadway and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or a siren approaches from behind, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the nearest curb or edge of the roadway and stop until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer. Do not speed up or block its path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm extended downward signify?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver intends to stop.
note: Hand and arm signals are used if your turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm extended straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward means a right turn, and a left arm extended downward means the driver is slowing or stopping. When you see a downward arm signal, be prepared to slow or stop.

question: What minimum following distance should you maintain under normal conditions?
options: a:A two-second space cushion.,b:A three-second space cushion.,c:200 feet at all times.
note: Under normal driving conditions, you should follow the vehicle ahead by at least a three-second gap. Pick a fixed object, and when the vehicle ahead passes it, you should be able to count at least "one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three" before you reach the same point. Increase this distance in bad weather, at higher speeds, or when following large vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a \No standing\" sign mean at a location?"
options: a:You may park there if you stay in the vehicle.,b:You may never stop your vehicle there for any reason.,c:You may stop temporarily only to load or discharge passengers.
note: A "No Standing" sign means you may stop only briefly to pick up or drop off passengers. You may not wait there, load or unload cargo, or park the vehicle. If you are not actively loading or unloading passengers, you must not stand in that area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a right turn, your vehicle should be positioned:
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:As far to the right side of the road as practicable.,c:Close to the left side of the road.
note: Before making a right turn, you should safely move your vehicle as close to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway as practicable. This positioning helps you turn into the correct lane, reduces the chance of cutting across lanes, and makes your intentions clear to other drivers and cyclists.

question: In foggy conditions, you should use your:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not bright enough and are not a substitute for headlights.

question: When driving at night and an oncoming vehicle approaches, your headlights should be:
options: a:Should be off. Use your parking lights.,b:Should be on their low beam setting.,c:Should be on their high beam setting.
note: When an oncoming vehicle approaches at night, switch to low beam headlights. High beams can blind the other driver and create a dangerous situation. Low beams give you enough light to see the road while reducing glare for other drivers. Parking lights alone are never enough for driving at night.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:If a crossing gate is lowered.,b:If the crossing lights are flashing.,c:If there is a stop sign, flashing red lights, a lowered gate, or a flagger signaling you to stop.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing whenever there is a stop sign, flashing red lights, a lowered gate, or a flagger signaling you to stop, even if you do not see or hear a train. These devices warn that a train may be approaching or is close enough to create danger, and you must obey them every time.

question: What actions reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster to get through wet patches quicker.,b:Use tires with improper air pressure to increase surface area.,c:Do not speed on wet roads and maintain proper tire pressure and tread.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce this risk, slow down on wet roads and make sure your tires are properly inflated and have good tread depth. Worn or underinflated tires and higher speeds greatly increase the chance of hydroplaning.

question: Which practice helps conserve gasoline while driving?
options: a:Accelerating quickly.,b:Sitting in your driveway with the engine running.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: To conserve fuel, accelerate smoothly, look ahead, and slow down gradually so you avoid unnecessary braking. Hard acceleration and frequent stopping waste gasoline. Idling the engine while parked also burns fuel without moving the vehicle, which is inefficient.

question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:
options: a:Dangerous.,b:Safe to cross at all times.,c:Places to park temporarily.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous because trains cannot stop quickly and may be hard to see or hear. Drivers should slow, look, listen, and obey all warning signs, lights, and gates before crossing the tracks.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation?
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Brown.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for guidance to recreational areas, parks, campgrounds, and points of cultural or historical interest. They help drivers find public recreation sites when traveling.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you pass them.,b:Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and leave as much space as possible—many states require at least 3 feet or more. Do not drive in the bike lane or honk aggressively, as this can startle the rider and cause a crash.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive through deeper puddles rather than skirt them.,b:Increase your speed gradually.,c:Drive more slowly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, which is more likely at higher speeds and in standing water. Reducing your speed and avoiding deep puddles greatly lowers the risk.

question: Why must you use increased caution while driving at night?
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night.,b:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.,c:There is more traffic at night.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge distance and see pedestrians, animals, and road hazards. Because you cannot see as well in the dark, you must use headlights and drive more cautiously.

question: What do highway pavement markings and signs provide for drivers?
options: a:They are only found in construction zones.,b:They provide information and guidance for safe driving.,c:They are usually not important.
note: Pavement markings and road signs give you important information about lane use, passing zones, turns, speed limits, and hazards so you can drive safely and predictably.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign typically warn you about?
options: a:Conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:The nearest towns and distances.,c:Traffic laws and regulations you must obey.
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert you to conditions or hazards on or near the road ahead so you can slow down or adjust your driving.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Cut them off to make them slow down.,c:Avoid eye contact and safely create distance.
note: When dealing with an aggressive driver, stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and safely create space between your vehicle and theirs. Do not engage, race, or retaliate, as that can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to stop at an intersection?
options: a:A steady yellow light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign, then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Parking or stopping on the shoulder of a freeway is allowed:
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.,c:Only in case of emergency.
note: On freeways, you may stop or park on the shoulder only for emergencies such as breakdowns or medical issues. Simply turning on hazard flashers or staying off the travel lane does not make non‑emergency stopping legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection,c:Slow down if comfortable.
note: A steady red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk, stop line, or entering the intersection, and remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed.

question: How would you classify distracted driving?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Nothing to worry about.,c:Extremely risky behavior.
note: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous because it takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving, greatly increasing the risk of a crash.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system hazardous?
options: a:It improves fuel economy.,b:It causes a loss of hearing.,c:It can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, enter the vehicle’s interior, which can quickly lead to serious illness or death if not repaired.

question: When driving on major highways, which habits should you maintain?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving and avoid fixed gaze.,b:All of the above.,c:Stay alert and be ready to react to hazards.
note: On major highways you should stay alert, keep your eyes moving instead of staring at one spot, and be ready to react quickly to changing traffic or sudden hazards.

question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:White
note: White lines—solid or broken—separate traffic moving in the same direction, while yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: Which statement about driving in changing weather is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires a change in driving habits.,b:You should always drive faster in rain and fog.,c:Be less aware of vehicles behind you in inclement weather.
note: Weather changes can quickly affect visibility and road traction. When rain, fog, snow, or wind begins or intensifies, you must adjust your driving: slow down, increase following distance, and stay especially aware of vehicles around you, including those behind that may not be slowing appropriately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following should you do when changing lanes?
options: a:Speed up suddenly and dart into the lane.,b:Signal only and rely on mirrors alone.,c:Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.
note: Safe lane changes require three steps working together: signal to let others know your intention, check your mirrors to see traffic beside and behind you, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never rely only on mirrors or sudden speed changes when moving into another lane.

question: When meeting a car with high beams that blind you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights on and off.,b:Use your high beams to return the glare.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road until it passes.
note: Oncoming high beams can temporarily blind you. Do not look directly at the lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide until the vehicle passes, while keeping your vehicle centered in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Single broken yellow line.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross it only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you may not use it to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are already inside an intersection and the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue carefully through the intersection.,b:Immediately reverse out of the intersection.,c:Stop in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely rather than stopping abruptly in the middle.

question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, what does it allow you to do?
options: a:Make a protected left turn without yielding.,b:Stop and wait for a green arrow before turning.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you are allowed to turn left, but your turn is not protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians, and only turn when it is safe and there is an adequate gap.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Only use your left side mirror.,b:Only use the rearview mirror.,c:Glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: Mirrors alone cannot show everything around your vehicle; there are blind spots to the sides that mirrors do not cover. Before changing lanes, you should quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check for vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles in your blind spot.

question: What is the best response to being tailgated?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to make them back off.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and them.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass.
note: When someone is following too closely, the safest response is to make it easier for them to pass you. If possible, change lanes safely or gradually slow down so they can go around you. Avoid sudden braking or speeding up, as these actions can increase the risk of a collision.

question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:
options: a:Are more likely to be distracted and make driving errors.,b:Are safer because they can focus better.,c:Have trouble driving slowly.
note: Eating or drinking while driving is a form of distraction because it takes at least one hand and some of your attention away from the driving task. Distracted drivers are more likely to make mistakes such as drifting out of their lane, following too closely, or reacting too slowly to hazards.

question: At a multi-track railroad crossing, after a train passes you should:
options: a:Cross immediately when the first train passes.,b:Stop on the first track and look for another train.,c:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.
note: At a multi-track railroad crossing, one train passing does not guarantee the other tracks are clear. After a train passes, wait until you can see down all tracks and confirm no other trains are approaching before you proceed across.

question: If another vehicle appears likely to hit you, what is an appropriate immediate action?
options: a:Turn off your headlights to avoid startling them.,b:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.,c:Wave your arms out the window to get their attention.
note: Using your horn is the correct immediate action when another vehicle may hit you. The horn is designed to warn other road users of imminent danger so they can react quickly. Do not turn off your headlights or wave your arms; those actions are less effective and can make the situation more dangerous.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane heading toward you, what should you do first?
options: a:Steer left into oncoming traffic to avoid the collision.,b:Accelerate straight ahead to pass it quickly.,c:Sound your horn.
note: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane, you should first try to get the other driver’s attention by sounding your horn, then move to the right and slow down or brake firmly. Never swerve left into oncoming traffic, because that puts you directly in the path of other vehicles and can cause a head‑on collision.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on all of the following EXCEPT:
options: a:How much you drink.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage.,d:The time you take to drink.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is determined by how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and how your body processes alcohol. The type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, or liquor) does not by itself determine BAC; what matters is the total amount of pure alcohol you take in over time.

question: What does defensive driving primarily involve?
options: a:Getting ahead of slower drivers to prevent conflicts.,b:Anticipating dangerous situations and taking actions to avoid accidents.,c:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance to reduce lane changes.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, anticipating possible hazards, and adjusting your speed or position early to avoid trouble. You should not tailgate or rush ahead of others; instead, you leave space and time to react safely to the unexpected.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the road, what should you do?
options: a:Jerk the wheel and force the car back onto the pavement quickly.,b:Speed up to get back on the road.,c:Keep a steady grip, slow down gradually with your wheels off the pavement, then gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.
note: If your wheels slip off the edge of the road, ease off the accelerator, keep a firm grip on the wheel, and steer straight while your wheels are off the pavement. Once you have slowed to a safe speed and the edge is clear, gently steer back onto the roadway. Jerking the wheel or speeding up can cause you to lose control or skid into traffic.

question: Before backing out of your driveway when children are nearby, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,b:Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.,c:Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: Before backing when children are nearby, you should get out and physically check behind your vehicle. Small children can be in blind spots that mirrors and cameras do not show. Walking to the back of the car ensures the area is clear before you move.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.,b:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.,c:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
note: On icy or snowy roads, you should slow down and leave much more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Lower speed and a longer following distance give you more time to react and help prevent skids and collisions on slippery surfaces.

question: Why should you be especially careful when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:The cyclist may swerve to avoid an object, creating a hazard.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You are moving faster than the bicycle so you don't need to be cautious.
note: When passing a bicyclist, be especially careful because they may need to swerve to avoid potholes, debris, or opening car doors. Always give cyclists plenty of space and pass only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,b:You must always avoid hitting pedestrians and be prepared to yield whenever they are in the roadway.,c:Only when the pedestrian uses a crosswalk.
note: Drivers must always do everything possible to avoid hitting pedestrians. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections, and you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians anywhere in the roadway, even if they are crossing illegally. The safest practice is to slow or stop whenever a pedestrian is in your path or could enter it.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It has no added risk beyond alcohol alone.,b:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It reduces alcohol's effects on driving ability.
note: Taking drugs together with alcohol greatly increases impairment. Many medications and illegal drugs interact with alcohol to slow your reactions, reduce coordination, and affect judgment, which raises the risk of a crash far beyond alcohol alone.

question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.,b:Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.,c:Winter is the most difficult driving season.
note: You should not use cruise control on snow, ice, or in other slippery winter conditions because it can cause you to lose traction and makes it harder to react quickly. In winter, it is especially important to check antifreeze and washer fluid and to recognize that winter is generally the most difficult driving season due to snow, ice, and reduced visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Maintain your current speed.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection faster.,c:Reduce your speed so you can maintain control.
note: Before and during a turn, you should slow to a safe speed so you can stay in your lane and maintain full control of the vehicle. Entering a turn too fast can cause skidding or drifting out of your lane, while accelerating into a turn reduces your ability to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:The driver plans to turn left.,b:The driver is planning to stop.,c:The driver plans to turn right.
note: Standard hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, arm bent upward for a right turn, and arm bent downward for slowing or stopping. Recognizing these signals is important when following vehicles such as bicycles or older vehicles that may not use electric turn signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The larger vehicle,c:The driver on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions; always proceed only when it is your turn and the intersection is clear.

question: If an approaching vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,b:Directly at the center of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide until the vehicle passes, which helps protect your night vision and keeps you in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is correct about turning at a steady red light?
options: a:You may make a U-turn anywhere unless a sign forbids it.,b:You may turn left on red only where specifically allowed by law (such as from a one-way street onto a one-way street) and after yielding.,c:You may turn right after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic unless otherwise posted.
note: At a steady red light, you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or limit line. Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn right after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and all cross traffic. Left turns on red are only allowed in limited situations (typically from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street where permitted by law and not prohibited by signs). U‑turns are never allowed "anywhere"; they are restricted by signs, markings, and visibility rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, what must you do regarding other road users?
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians unless signaled otherwise.,c:Proceed quickly because you have the right-of-way.
note: When making a left turn, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only proceed when there is a safe gap and when traffic signals, signs, or a traffic officer indicate it is your turn to go.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Get some coffee.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Open your window and continue driving.
note: If you feel tired while driving, the safest choice is to stop driving and rest. Short-term tricks like coffee or opening a window do not reliably prevent drowsiness and can give a false sense of alertness. Plan to pull over in a safe place and rest or change drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection after slowing and scanning for hazards.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, scan the intersection carefully, and be prepared to yield to other vehicles and pedestrians. Do not stop unless needed for safety; continue through only when it is clearly safe.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When the train has passed.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. Even if a train has passed, another train may be coming, and signals may still be active. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised before crossing the tracks.

question: How should you reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night?
options: a:Turn on your interior lights to reduce glare.,b:Look straight ahead at the oncoming headlights.,c:Look toward the right side of the road ahead and avoid staring at the lights.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To protect your night vision, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide instead of looking directly at the lights. Do not turn on interior lights or stare at the oncoming headlights, as both make it harder to see the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles merging onto a freeway?
options: a:Safely merge out of the right lane to allow them access.,b:Always drive in the far left lane.,c:Abruptly slow to let them in.
note: On freeways, smooth merging keeps traffic flowing and reduces crashes. When you see vehicles entering from an on‑ramp, and it is safe, move out of the right lane to give them space to merge. If you cannot change lanes, maintain a steady speed when possible and avoid sudden braking that could surprise drivers behind you.

question: When parking parallel to a curb, you must park within:
options: a:Park within 18 inches of the curb or edge of the roadway.,b:Park facing oncoming traffic.,c:Park within 24 inches of the curb or edge of the roadway.
note: Park parallel and within 18 inches of the curb or edge of the roadway, facing the same direction as traffic on that side of the street.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:Deaf.,b:Part of a traffic study.,c:A blind pedestrian.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. You must always yield the right‑of‑way, stop well before the crosswalk, and never honk or rev your engine, as this can startle the person or the guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which has priority over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A steady red light.,c:A police officer directing traffic.
note: A police officer or other authorized person directing traffic has priority over all traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings. If their directions conflict with a light or sign, you must follow the officer’s instructions to keep traffic moving safely and orderly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:
options: a:Flash your lights.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: You must always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk. Slow down early and be ready to stop so the pedestrian can cross safely. Never try to intimidate them by flashing lights or speeding up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you need to turn but are in the wrong lane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.,b:Turn from your current lane after signaling.,c:Cut across traffic quickly to make the turn.
note: If you are in the wrong lane for a turn, continue straight and go to the next intersection. Sudden lane changes or turns from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a street that has multiple lanes traveling in your direction, where should you end up?
options: a:In the middle lane.,b:In the lane closest to the lane you were in before the turn.,c:In any lane you choose after turning.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane road, you must turn into the lane that is directly next to the one you came from. This keeps traffic predictable and prevents sideswipe collisions with vehicles turning beside you.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Wet roads do not cause hydroplaning.,b:Pavement can be especially slippery right after rain begins.,c:You should always follow the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: When rain first begins, water mixes with oil and dirt on the road, making the surface especially slippery. Slow down, increase following distance, and be gentle with steering and braking to avoid skids and hydroplaning.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Proceed slowly and let it pass in traffic.,b:Stop immediately in your current lane.,c:Drive as far right as safely possible and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must move as far to the right as safely possible and stop until it passes. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in Idaho, what speed principle must you follow?
options: a:Always drive 10 mph below the posted limit.,b:Drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: You must drive at a speed that is safe for current road, weather, and traffic conditions even if it is below the posted limit.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass if safe.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross it only to turn left into or from a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your safety?
options: a:It has no effect on driving abilities.,b:It helps maintain driver alertness.,c:It is a distracting activity that can reduce driving performance.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction. It takes at least one hand off the wheel and your eyes and attention away from the road to handle lighters, matches, or cigarettes. Any activity that divides your attention can slow your reaction time and increase the risk of a crash.

question: What should a driver do upon seeing an animal on the roadway?
options: a:Pass the animal slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.,b:Pass closely to minimize delay.,c:Ignore it and maintain speed.
note: When you see an animal on or near the roadway, slow down and be prepared to stop. Passing slowly and giving the animal space helps avoid startling it, which could cause it to dart into your path or into other traffic. Use extra caution at night or in rural areas where animals are more common.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and then proceed when safe.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to other vehicles and pedestrians. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to traffic already on the freeway.,b:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.,c:Use the acceleration lane to match speed to freeway traffic.
note: When merging onto a freeway, you must do three things together: use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches freeway traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Freeway traffic has the right‑of‑way, so you adjust your speed and wait for a safe gap before merging.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus displaying its stop arm and flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass carefully if no children are visible.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This applies on most roads in both directions unless you are on a divided highway with a physical median and your lane is opposite the bus. Children may cross unexpectedly, so you must not pass the bus while the signals are active.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which rule is a good guideline to remember about passing?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,b:Pass on the right whenever possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to see better.
note: Passing always carries extra risk because you move into another lane and may face oncoming traffic or blind spots. A safe guideline is to drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and pass only when it is truly necessary and clearly safe, with enough space and visibility to complete the maneuver without speeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to other drivers under which circumstance listed?
options: a:Only where a yield sign is present.,b:Only when you want to yield.,c:When workers are present in construction zones.
note: You must always yield and use extra caution in construction and work zones. Slow down, obey posted signs and flaggers, and be prepared to stop or let workers and construction vehicles go first. Work zones often have changing traffic patterns and workers close to moving vehicles, so yielding and reducing speed greatly improves safety.

question: At a light rail intersection you should always:
options: a:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Look both ways before crossing tracks.,c:Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
note: At light rail intersections, always pay close attention and obey all traffic signals, signs, and crossing gates. Never drive around lowered gates or ignore flashing lights. Trains are fast, quiet, and cannot stop quickly, so you must follow the signals and also look both ways before crossing or turning across the tracks.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing tracks with no gates or signals, what should you ensure before entering?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:There is room for your vehicle to get all the way across the tracks without stopping.
note: Before you drive onto railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks without stopping. Never stop on the tracks and never pass other vehicles while crossing.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, what are drivers allowed to do?
options: a:Merge into the lane indicated without yielding.,b:Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.,c:Stop and wait for a circular green.
note: A steady green arrow means you may turn only in the direction of the arrow. This is a protected turn, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection before completing your turn.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do?
options: a:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.
note: If someone is injured in a crash, do not move them unless there is immediate danger, such as fire or risk of another collision. Moving an injured person can worsen their injuries. Keep them warm, reassure them, call 911, and give first aid only if you are trained.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in the roadway to view the accident.,b:Drive to the scene and get out to take photos.,c:Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived; otherwise keep moving and stay alert.
note: When approaching a crash scene, do not slow or stop just to look. This creates additional hazards and congestion. Only stop if you are directly involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist. Otherwise, continue carefully and stay alert for people and emergency vehicles.

question: What do working brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:You are about to turn.,b:You have your emergency brake on.,c:You are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. Keeping your brake lights in good working order helps prevent rear-end collisions by giving others time to react.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using its lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using its lights or siren, you must immediately pull as far to the right as you safely can and stop until it has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely. You should not just slow down and keep going in your lane.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lights should you use?
options: a:Turn on emergency flashers and keep low-beam headlights on.,b:Turn off all lights.,c:Use only parking lights.
note: If you must stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low‑beam headlights on. This makes your vehicle clearly visible to other drivers without blinding them, reducing the risk of a collision with your stopped vehicle.

question: When driving on an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Always use cruise control.,b:Signal before changing lanes and check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
note: Before changing lanes on an interstate, you must signal to let other drivers know your intention, then check your mirrors and blind spots and change lanes only when it is safe. Cruise control is optional and unrelated to lane changes, and you should only stop on the shoulder for emergencies, not just because you are tired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, what should you do?
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
note: On a narrow two‑way road, you must allow the oncoming vehicle at least one‑half of the main‑traveled portion of the roadway so both vehicles can pass safely. Slow down and keep as far to the right as is safe, but you do not need to leave the roadway unless required to avoid a collision.

question: Double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean:
options: a:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only when making a permitted left turn or when specifically allowed by law, but you must not use the opposing lane to pass other vehicles.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, when one train clears you should:
options: a:Proceed immediately after one train passes.,b:Look for another train on the other track before crossing.,c:Always stop before crossing.
note: When there are multiple railroad tracks, a second train can approach on the other track, sometimes from the opposite direction, right after the first train passes. After one train clears, stop, look, and listen carefully for another train on any adjacent track before you proceed across.

question: Which of the following is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are making quick and sudden stops.,b:They are weaving between lanes.,c:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,d:All of the above.
note: Impaired drivers often show several warning behaviors, including weaving, sudden stops, and driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic for no clear reason. Any of these can be a sign of drunk driving and should be reported, but driving significantly below the normal speed without cause is one of the most commonly noted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited:
options: a:At intersections.,b:On hills and curves.,c:All of the above.,d:Only when there is a solid yellow line.
note: Passing is unsafe and illegal in places like hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where you cannot see oncoming traffic clearly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Bicyclists in the roundabout.,b:Pedestrians in the crosswalks at the roundabout.,c:Vehicles already in the roundabout.,d:All of the above.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to all traffic already in the circle, as well as to pedestrians in crosswalks and bicyclists using the roundabout or its approaches. Vehicles in the roundabout have the right-of-way, and you must wait for a safe gap while also checking for and yielding to people walking or biking.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Get out and walk for help immediately.,b:Lie down in the car and go to sleep.,c:Stay in your car and wait for help
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, staying in your vehicle is usually the safest choice. Your car provides shelter from cold and wind and makes it easier for rescuers to find you. Run the engine only periodically for heat, make sure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow, and keep a window slightly open for fresh air while you wait for help.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:Less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you cannot see as far ahead, it is harder to judge speed and distance, and glare from headlights plus fatigue can slow your reaction time. You must drive more carefully and often more slowly at night.

question: Which parking scenario is allowed based on distance rules?
options: a:Parking too close to a fire hydrant (typically within about 15 feet).,b:Parking about 25 feet away from a crosswalk at an intersection.,c:Parking on a sidewalk or blocking pedestrian paths.
note: Parking too close to a fire hydrant or crosswalk blocks access and visibility. In many states you must not park within about 15 feet of a fire hydrant or within about 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection. Parking 25 feet from a crosswalk is generally allowed because it keeps the crossing area clear for pedestrians and improves sight lines for drivers.

question: When is it permissible to cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:Only to make a turn into a driveway or side street.,c:At any time.
note: A solid yellow center line means no passing other vehicles in the opposite lane. However, you may cross a solid yellow line when you are turning left into or out of a driveway, alley, or side street, as long as it is safe and not otherwise prohibited by signs.

question: A driver who drives much slower than the posted speed limit is generally:
options: a:Potentially hazardous and may be required to pull over if causing a backup.,b:A very safe driver.,c:Always has the right-of-way.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because faster drivers may have to brake or change lanes suddenly. On many two-lane roads, if you are holding up several vehicles, you are required to pull over at a safe place and let them pass.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones ahead.,c:Railroad crossings; yield to trains.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It acts like a yield sign: you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If a train is approaching, you must yield and never try to beat the train through the crossing.

question: The single most effective thing to reduce your risk of injury in a crash is to:
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Limit your driving to weekdays.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and help you stay in position to maintain control.

question: A single dashed yellow centerline means:
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may not pass.,c:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
note: A single dashed (broken) yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is broken on your side, you may cross it to pass another vehicle if you can do so safely and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid red arrow signal indicate?
options: a:It indicates a pedestrian crossing only.,b:The arrow means you may turn after yielding.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular red light — stop and do not turn in the arrow's direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped. You may not make the movement in the direction of the arrow until it turns green or is replaced by a signal that allows that movement, just as you would obey a circular red light for that direction.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Keep driving normally until you find a service area.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly to keep control and stay in your lane. Ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually, then when you are moving slowly, apply the brakes gently and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, what must a driver produce?
options: a:Only proof of insurance.,b:Only registration.,c:Driver's license, registration, and proof of insurance
note: When stopped by law enforcement, you must be able to show your driver’s license, the vehicle’s registration, and valid proof of insurance. These documents verify that you are legally allowed to drive and that the vehicle is properly registered and insured.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when you get to an intersection showing a flashing red light?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.,b:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.,c:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If someone has consumed alcohol, which will help them overcome its influence?
options: a:Only time,b:Hot coffee,c:Fresh air
note: Once alcohol is in the bloodstream, only time allows your body to metabolize it and reduce impairment. Coffee, fresh air, cold showers, or exercise may make a person feel more awake, but they do not speed up the elimination of alcohol or make driving safe.

question: Which devices are sometimes used to direct drivers into the correct turning lanes on highways?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:White lines on the side of the road only.,c:Arrow markings and lane-control arrows.
note: Arrow markings painted on the pavement and lane‑control arrows on overhead or roadside signs show which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. Following these arrows helps you be in the correct lane before you reach the intersection or exit.

question: What must you do if you are leaving your vehicle unattended?
options: a:Leave the engine running briefly while you run a quick errand.,b:Only set the parking brake.,c:Lock the ignition and remove the key from the vehicle.
note: When leaving a vehicle, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake to help prevent theft or unintended movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and continue without stopping.,b:Merge to the right.,c:Come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red signal means you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or close to the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow line next to your lane indicate?
options: a:You may pass with caution.,b:Do not pass from your direction.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you must not cross it to pass other vehicles from your direction. It separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing would be unsafe, so you must stay in your lane.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the road between the cars.
note: You should avoid following too closely because you may not have enough time and distance to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. A safe following distance gives you room to react and brake smoothly, helping prevent rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:You see a police car.,b:Entering a highway where there are other cars.,c:Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. When rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions make driving less than ideal, you must slow down below the posted limit so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: How should a properly adjusted lap belt fit?
options: a:Hidden beneath the seat so it does not show.,b:Loose for more comfort.,c:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
note: A lap belt should be worn low and snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen, not across your stomach. This position helps the belt hold your body securely in a crash and reduces the risk of internal injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to other drivers when:
options: a:Your traffic signal is a green arrow.,b:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.,c:When entering a street from a garage or alley.
note: When you enter a street from a driveway, alley, or garage, you must stop if necessary and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road. At unmarked intersections, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right when both arrive at the same time.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a collision, what is the correct action?
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible.,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police before moving the vehicle.
note: If your vehicle is drivable and no one is seriously injured, you should move it out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional crashes and keeps traffic flowing. You must still stay at the scene, exchange information, and assist anyone who is injured.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Flash your lights at the driver to make them look.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,c:Never pass them under any circumstances.
note: Trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. To stay safe, avoid driving right alongside these vehicles for long periods and never follow too closely. If you cannot see the truck or bus driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you.

question: When stopped on an incline, you should allow a larger space cushion in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:The vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic moves again.,b:It is required by law to stop farther back.,c:You should always leave extra room only at stop signs.
note: On hills, the vehicle in front of you may roll backward when starting to move again. Leaving extra space in front of your vehicle gives you room to react and helps you avoid a rear-end collision if the other driver’s car rolls back.

question: Which of the following are important steps to drive safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance, ensure headlights are working, and avoid driving when tired.,b:Use high beam headlights at all times.,c:Drive faster to make the trip shorter.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to see hazards. Increasing your following distance gives you more time to react. Making sure your headlights work properly improves what you can see and how well others see you. Avoid driving when you are tired because fatigue slows your reaction time and can lead to drowsy driving.

question: At a railroad crossing marked only with a crossbuck (no lights or gates), what is the safe approach?
options: a:Always stop before crossing even if no train is coming.,b:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,c:Speed across quickly to avoid stalling.
note: At a crossing with only a crossbuck, you must slow down, look, and listen carefully for trains. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space on the far side of the tracks for your vehicle to clear the crossing completely without stopping on the tracks.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement typically mean?
options: a:Drivers in the lane may ignore the arrow without consequence.,b:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must come to a complete stop before using the arrow lane.
note: Pavement arrows tell you what movement is allowed or required from that lane, such as straight, left turn, or right turn. You must follow the direction of the arrow unless a sign or signal clearly allows something different.

question: For drivers 21 and older in Idaho, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) defines driving under the influence?
options: a:0.02 percent or higher.,b:0.04 percent or higher.,c:0.08 percent or higher.
note: For drivers 21 and older in Idaho, a BAC of 0.08% or higher is considered driving under the influence. Commercial drivers have a lower limit (0.04%), and drivers under 21 are subject to a much lower BAC limit, but for standard adult drivers the legal DUI threshold is 0.08%.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Immediately after passing regardless of space.,c:Only when you intend to turn left.
note: When passing on a two-lane road, you should return to your lane only when you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe space cushion between you. Cutting back too soon can force the other driver to brake or create a rear-end collision risk.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what is the safest move?
options: a:Stay in the blind spot and maintain speed.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Flash your lights constantly.
note: Blind spots are areas where you are not visible in another driver’s mirrors. It is unsafe to linger there. Either move ahead to pass safely or slow down to fall back so that the other driver can clearly see your vehicle in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who may adjust speed limits in specific areas by posting speed limit signs?
options: a:Only the state government can post varying speed limits.,b:State and local authorities by posting speed limit signs.,c:No one; speed limits are the same everywhere.
note: Speed limits are set and posted by state and local authorities based on road type, traffic, and safety studies. You must obey the posted speed limit for the specific road you are on, even if it differs from nearby roads.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Check mirrors and signal.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, signal, and quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when the lane is clear and adjust your speed smoothly so you don’t cut off other drivers.

question: Where on the roadway are you most likely to encounter ice that freezes quickly in cold or wet weather?
options: a:On flat, open sections of road,b:Shaded areas such as those under trees or next to buildings.,c:On the sunny side of the road.
note: Shaded areas such as those under trees, on bridges, or next to buildings stay colder and lose sunlight, so they freeze first and stay icy longer than open, sunny pavement. Always slow down and be extra cautious in these spots during cold or wet weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about speed is correct?
options: a:Speeding always reduces crash risk.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
