note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic on certain highways can be dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing the risk of rear‑end and sideswipe crashes. Safe driving means matching the legal speed to road, traffic, and weather conditions—not going too fast or too slow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is permitted while stopped in a travel lane on the roadway?
options: a:Stop to drop off passengers.,b:Make a U-turn or back up if you missed your exit.,c:None of these — you should not stop in a travel lane.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane except in emergencies or when required by traffic or signals. Stopping to drop off passengers, backing up, or making U‑turns from a travel lane is unsafe and often illegal; instead, continue to a safe place off the roadway.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow but the main light is red, what does that mean?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,b:You may only drive straight ahead.,c:You may drive only in the direction the green arrow indicates.
note: A green arrow means you are allowed to move only in the direction the arrow points, even if the main signal is red. Enter the intersection carefully, yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection, and complete your turn only in that indicated direction.

question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to make others aware of you.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: Looking well ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you time to see problems early and slow down smoothly instead of slamming on the brakes. This reduces the need for sudden emergency stops and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: If followed by a fire engine that is not using its emergency signals on a two-lane street, you should:
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop as quickly as you can.
note: Emergency vehicles that are not using lights or sirens are not requesting the right-of-way. You should obey normal traffic laws and continue driving in a safe, predictable manner without speeding up or stopping suddenly.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop when safe.,b:Try to reach your destination before it arrives.,c:Continue driving but avoid the emergency vehicle.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right as you safely can and stopping until it passes. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
note: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a fluorescent or reflective orange triangle with a red border mounted on the rear of vehicles that usually travel 25 mph or less. It warns faster traffic to approach and pass with caution.

question: What must a driver do when pedestrians are in crosswalks marked by two solid white lines?
options: a:Proceed only if the pedestrian steps away.,b:Yield and give the right-of-way to those pedestrians.,c:Drive through because vehicles have the right-of-way.
note: At marked crosswalks, pedestrians have the right-of-way. You must slow or stop as needed and allow pedestrians to fully cross your lane before proceeding, even if this means waiting until they are safely out of the crosswalk.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest way to pass a bicyclist traveling in your direction?
options: a:Continue straight; the bicyclist should get out of the way.,b:Never pass until you reach a signal or stop sign.,c:Wait until no oncoming traffic is present, then change lanes or move over to give the bicyclist at least 3 feet of space before passing.
note: On a two-lane road without a bike lane, you should pass a bicyclist the same way you would pass a slow-moving vehicle: wait until there is no oncoming traffic, move into the opposite lane if needed, and leave at least 3 feet of clearance (or more if required by your state). Do not squeeze past in the same lane; instead, wait for a safe gap, change lanes or move over, and then pass at a safe speed.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in or close to the intersection.

question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:
options: a:When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing red or blue lights, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as you safely can to the right edge of the road and stopping until the vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed by a police officer.

question: When faced with an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right, what should you do?
options: a:Drive between them (split the difference).,b:Slow down and let the oncoming car pass before safely passing the bicyclist.,c:Pull onto the shoulder immediately.
note: When you have an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, do not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first so you only deal with one hazard at a time. After the oncoming car has passed and the opposing lane is clear, move over to give the bicyclist plenty of space and then pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A solid red light.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Drivers of motor vehicles must yield to a pedestrian under which conditions?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is elderly,b:When the pedestrian is crossing or about to cross within a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in or about to enter a marked or unmarked crosswalk. You must be prepared to stop whenever pedestrians are present, regardless of their age or the time of day.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously at an open (uncontrolled) intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Either may proceed without yielding.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your vehicle, what is the correct action?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce speed and stay in your lane to allow safe passing.,b:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.,c:Pull off the road.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane, maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce speed, and allow them to pass safely. Do not speed up or signal them when to pass; they are responsible for deciding when it is safe to complete the maneuver.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,c:Brake hard immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and slowly ease your foot off the accelerator. Once the vehicle has slowed and you have control, apply the brakes gently and move off the road to a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back slightly until the tire gently touches the curb. This way, if your brakes fail, the curb will stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: What does a steady green arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to vehicles/pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:It has no different meaning from a circular green.,c:You must stop and wait for a circular green.
note: A steady green arrow means you are allowed to proceed only in the direction of the arrow. You must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection or still clearing it before you move.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive safely?
options: a:Only lack of sleep.,b:Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and fatigue.,c:Only illegal drugs.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, legal prescription or over‑the‑counter drugs, illegal drugs, and fatigue. Any substance or condition that affects your judgment, reaction time, or alertness makes driving unsafe, so you must never assume only one factor is dangerous.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and follow loudspeaker instructions.,b:Ignore it if you are not in its lane.,c:Continue driving normally.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way by pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping when safe. Follow any instructions given over a loudspeaker and stay alert, as more emergency vehicles may follow.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following behaviors?
options: a:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,b:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
note: Many crashes happen because drivers travel too fast for conditions, even if they are at or below the posted speed limit. You must adjust your speed for rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, curves, and poor road surfaces to maintain control and enough time to react.

question: When changing lanes to the left, where should you glance to check your blind spot?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:Over your left shoulder.,c:At your side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Looking over your left shoulder checks the left‑side blind spot that your mirrors cannot show when moving into the left lane.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you always do first?
options: a:Continue driving if the damage seems minor.,b:Leave the scene and report later.,c:Stop at or near the scene and remain safe
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, check for immediate danger, and move yourself and your vehicle to a safe place if possible. Never leave the scene; staying there safely allows you to exchange information, help anyone who is injured, and comply with the law.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Check only your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles only.,c:Check your side view mirror and rearview mirror and glance over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview mirror and side mirror to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you’re moving to check your blind spot. Only move when the lane is clear and you have enough space.

question: To avoid driving unsafely because of health, you should:
options: a:Drive within your physical limitations.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,c:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.
note: Safe driving depends on your overall health. Staying physically fit, having regular medical checkups, and talking with your doctor about how any conditions or medications affect you helps you know whether it is safe to drive at all. You should not drive if your health or medicine makes it unsafe, regardless of your usual physical limitations.

question: Pentagonal-shaped road signs are used to indicate what?
options: a:School zones or school crossings.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pentagon-shaped signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

question: Which statement about drowsy driving is true?
options: a:Drinking coffee always makes a drowsy driver safe to continue.,b:Opening a window will keep you alert enough to drive safely.,c:Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated.
note: Drowsy drivers can be as impaired as drunk drivers: their reaction time, judgment, and attention are greatly reduced, and they may drift between lanes or even fall asleep. Short-term tricks like coffee or opening a window do not make it safe to continue; the real solution is to rest before driving.

question: What are the colors of signs that indicate distances to upcoming highway exits?
options: a:Green with white letters,b:Yellow with black letters,c:Red with white letters
note: Guide signs that show directions, destinations, and distances on highways are green with white letters or symbols. These signs help drivers navigate to exits, cities, and services.

question: If your vehicle hits an unattended parked car and you cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Must stay until the police arrive.,b:Leave a written notice with your name,c:Have done as much as you can.
note: If you hit a parked, unattended vehicle, you must stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a written note with your name, contact information, and a brief description of what happened. In many states you must also report the crash to police if damage meets the legal reporting threshold.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, how should you proceed?
options: a:Speed up to pass before they reach your lane.,b:Honk and continue through the intersection.,c:Stop to allow the pedestrians to cross safely.
note: You must always yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk, even if they are crossing against the signal and you have a green light. Stop and wait until they have safely cleared your path before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Watch for oncoming traffic.,b:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,c:Pass only on the right.
note: On a multilane highway, you normally pass on the left. Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear, check your mirrors and blind spot, signal, then move into the passing lane. Passing on the right is allowed only in specific situations and is not the general rule.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Excessive speed under the driving conditions.,b:Following other vehicles too closely,c:Inattentive driving
note: Driving too fast for road, traffic, or weather conditions is a major cause of crashes. Inattentive driving and following too closely are also common causes, which is why you should always adjust your speed, maintain a safe following distance, and stay focused on the road.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Only an airbag.,b:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,c:Only a lap and shoulder belt.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both the lap/shoulder belt and the airbag together. Seat belts keep you properly positioned and prevent you from being thrown forward, while airbags provide extra cushioning in certain types of collisions, especially front-end crashes. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them.

question: What typically causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Sudden turns only.,b:Stopping suddenly.,c:Driving too fast for wet conditions
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast for wet conditions and your tires ride up on a thin layer of water instead of gripping the road. This loss of traction can cause you to lose steering and braking control. Slowing down on wet roads and having good tire tread greatly reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:To pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.,b:Never under any circumstances.,c:Only to make a U-turn.
note: A single broken line means you may cross it to pass or change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so. You must check traffic, signal, and be sure you will not interfere with oncoming vehicles or vehicles behind you. Solid lines, in contrast, usually mean passing or lane changes are restricted or prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road, you should:
options: a:Stop and yield to pedestrians and vehicles on the roadway, entering only when it is safe.,b:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.,c:Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must stop if necessary and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. Do not pull out quickly, block the lane, or use your horn to force others to slow down. Enter only when there is a large enough gap so you can join traffic smoothly without making others brake or swerve.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Shift to park immediately.,b:Reach down and try to pull the accelerator up.,c:Shift the car into neutral and apply steady pressure to the brakes.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep looking at the road, shift the transmission into neutral, and apply steady, firm pressure to the brakes. Steer to a safe place off the road, then stop and turn off the engine. Do not turn the ignition off while moving, and do not reach down to pull on the pedal, because you could lose steering control.

question: Which of the following is a common effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:It slows your reaction time.,b:It improves your coordination.,c:It increases your ability to judge distance.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and nervous system function. When you drink, your reaction time gets slower, your coordination and judgment get worse, and your ability to estimate speed and distance is reduced. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair driving and increase crash risk.

question: The most common color of warning signs is:
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or words. They alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other hazards ahead so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: Increasing your vehicle's speed:
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Decreases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows and you see less to the sides (tunnel vision). This makes it harder to detect hazards, pedestrians, and cross traffic. Slowing down gives you a wider view and more time to react.

question: What is the primary safety benefit of wearing a seat belt?
options: a:Helps maintain control of the vehicle on winding roads.,b:Helps maintain control of the vehicle on rough roads.,c:Reduces the risk of injury or death in a crash.
note: Seat belts are designed to keep you inside the vehicle and spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body. This greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death in a collision and helps keep you properly positioned behind the wheel.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.,b:Make you drowsy while driving.,c:Cause excessive oil use.
note: A leaking exhaust system can allow carbon monoxide and other toxic gases to enter the passenger compartment. Breathing these fumes can make you drowsy, confused, or even unconscious, which is extremely dangerous while driving. Exhaust leaks should be repaired immediately.

question: Car drivers should remember that large trucks:
options: a:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,b:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,c:Have large blind spots.
note: Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly behind them, along both sides, and close in front of the cab. Because the driver cannot see you in these areas, you should avoid lingering beside or close behind a truck and make sure you can see the truck’s mirrors so the driver can see you.

question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Should slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending and a red arrow is coming. You should slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are already in the intersection when the light changes, complete your turn carefully.

question: Anything that requires you to ___ could cause you to crash.
options: a:Only take your hands off the wheel.,b:Take your attention away from driving.,c:Take only your eyes off the road.
note: Anything that takes your attention away from driving—such as texting, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers—can lead to a crash. Safe driving requires your full attention, including your eyes on the road, hands on the wheel, and mind focused on driving.

question: What are common effects of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:Improved reaction time.,b:Increased alertness.,c:Loss of concentration
note: Alcohol slows your reaction time and impairs judgment, concentration, coordination, and vision. Even small amounts make it harder to stay focused, react to hazards, and control your vehicle, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers should allow for:
options: a:Reduced noise levels from the truck.,b:Decreased stopping distance for large vehicles.,c:The increased stopping distance the truck requires.
note: Heavy trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop. When driving near trucks, leave extra space in front of them, avoid cutting in too closely, and do not brake suddenly in front of a truck.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should you do regarding other drivers?
options: a:You may force your way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:You have the right-of-way.
note: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the public roadway. Wait until there is a safe gap and then merge smoothly; you never have the right-of-way over vehicles already on the road.

question: Your vehicle's blind spot is the area:
options: a:You see in the rearview mirror.,b:You cannot see without turning your head.,c:Directly behind your vehicle only.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see with your mirrors alone. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an unmarked intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle that honks first.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect when you can afford it.,b:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,c:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can fix it.
note: Any defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle should be repaired as soon as possible. Driving with safety-related problems, even at lower speeds, increases your risk of a crash and may be illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Go to the next exit.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm and continue driving to the next exit. Do not stop, back up on the shoulder, or make a U-turn on the freeway, as these actions are extremely dangerous and usually illegal.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage change how significantly alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Beer impairs much less than wine.,b:No — any type of alcohol can impair reflexes and judgment depending on amount consumed.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks are always worse.
note: Alcohol’s effect on your body depends on how much pure alcohol you consume and your blood alcohol concentration (BAC), not whether it comes from beer, wine, or liquor. Any alcoholic drink with the same amount of alcohol can equally impair reflexes and judgment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slower vehicle.,c:To change lanes at any time.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and generally mean no passing. However, you may carefully cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make a permitted left turn or U‑turn when it is safe and legal.

question: A stop sign is shaped like which of the following?
options: a:Square.,b:Rectangle.,c:Octagon.
note: A stop sign has a unique octagon (eight‑sided) shape so drivers can recognize it quickly, even from the back or in poor visibility. When you see a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn a pedestrian or driver of imminent danger, such as a child about to run into the street.,b:While travelling through an intersection to hurry traffic.,c:While passing a bicyclist at normal safe distance.
note: Use your horn only as a warning to help prevent a collision, such as when another road user is about to move into your path and may not see you. It should not be used to express anger, hurry other drivers, or unnecessarily startle pedestrians or bicyclists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time from different highways, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Both may proceed without yielding.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive your vehicle at a speed greater than:
options: a:The minimum speed limit.,b:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions (and within legal limits).,c:The posted maximum speed only.
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that is below the posted speed limit. The posted maximum is the legal upper limit in ideal conditions; you must slow down for rain, fog, traffic, or poor road surfaces.

question: On average, how quickly does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:Two drinks per hour.,b:About one standard drink per hour.,c:Three drinks per hour.
note: The body typically processes alcohol at about the rate of one standard drink per hour. This is only an average; body size, sex, food, medications, and health can make the rate slower, so you can still be impaired even if you think enough time has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An advisory or restriction speed sign:
options: a:Has a yellow background with black lettering and is usually posted with a warning sign.,b:Is blue with black lettering.,c:May be ignored in rainy conditions.
note: Advisory or recommended speed signs are usually small rectangular plaques with a yellow background and black numbers, posted under a warning sign (such as a curve sign). They show a safe speed for that specific condition, not a mandatory limit, but you should follow them and slow even more when conditions are poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, you should:
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: When you are waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight ahead and your turn signal on. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels help prevent your car from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,b:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,c:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: When entering a street from a driveway or alley, you must come to a complete stop before the sidewalk or curb line, yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk, and yield to all approaching traffic on the street. Proceed only when it is safe and clear.

question: Which factor(s) affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:All of the above.,c:The condition of your brakes and tires.
note: Braking distance increases as your speed increases and when your brakes or tires are in poor condition. Good tires and brakes help you stop more quickly, while worn parts lengthen the distance needed to stop. Road surface and weather also affect braking distance, so you should always adjust your speed and following distance to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what is the first positioning step?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the open space before backing in.
note: For standard parallel parking, after you signal and check traffic, you first pull up so your vehicle is parallel and even with the vehicle in front of the open space. From this position, you then begin backing slowly while turning the wheel as needed to move into the space.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may not pass.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII arrest?
options: a:Only beer and wine.,b:Only prescription medicines.,c:Alcohol, illegal drugs, and many legal medications
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, and many legal medications, including some prescriptions and over‑the‑counter drugs. Any substance that affects your judgment, coordination, or reaction time can lead to a DUI/DWI arrest if it impairs your ability to drive safely.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping:
options: a:When driving at night.,b:On a wet or icy road.,c:On paved highways.
note: Stopping distance becomes longer on wet, icy, snowy, or loose‑surface roads because your tires have less traction. In these conditions you should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more space and time to stop safely.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Always stop whether or not a stop sign is present.,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Watch carefully for children and be ready to stop.
note: At a school crossing sign, slow down, scan carefully for children who may enter the road unexpectedly, and be ready to stop even if there is no stop sign. Children can be unpredictable, so you must drive cautiously and yield to anyone in the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your current lane.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach your exit.,c:Continue to the next exit or location where you can safely turn around.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm, continue driving to the next exit, and then find a safe way to turn around or re-route. Never stop, back up on the shoulder, or make sudden lane changes, because those actions can cause serious crashes at freeway speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, you are on:
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:A one-way road.,c:A two-way road.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic on the road is moving in opposite directions, so it is a two-way road. The broken line allows passing when it is safe and legal, but you must watch for oncoming traffic before crossing the centerline.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following should you do when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Rely solely on your mirrors.,b:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,c:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, signal in advance to warn other drivers, then check your mirrors and blind spots and move only when the lane is clear. Do not rely only on mirrors, and do not start signaling at the same moment you move; other drivers need time to react.

question: A solid white edge line that angles toward the left means:
options: a:There is an intersection immediately ahead.,b:You will be required to turn left just ahead.,c:The roadway is narrowing ahead.
note: A solid white edge line that angles toward the center of the road warns that the usable roadway is narrowing. You should be prepared for less space, adjust your speed if needed, and stay within your lane to avoid drifting off the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and other road users already in the intersection.,b:Only to vehicles behind you.,c:Only to pedestrians who are off the curb.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic and to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection. Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right have the right-of-way, and you may only complete your turn when it is safe and clear.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should the driver of a small vehicle be prepared for?
options: a:Only visual obstructions,b:Loud music from the large vehicle.,c:Wind gusts that can change the small vehicle's direction.
note: Large trucks and buses create strong air turbulence. As you pass or are passed by a large vehicle, wind gusts can push or pull your smaller vehicle sideways. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to make small steering corrections to stay in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived first.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The driver who does not stop.
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive and stop has the right-of-way and goes first. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. All drivers must come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp correctly?
options: a:Keep your speed on the freeway until you are in the exit lane or on the exit ramp, then slow to the posted ramp or safe speed.,b:Begin braking hard on the freeway well before the exit.,c:Slow to city-street speeds while still in the freeway travel lane before exiting.
note: On a freeway, you should stay at freeway speed until you are actually in the exit lane or on the exit ramp, so you do not disrupt fast-moving traffic behind you. Once you are fully on the ramp, then slow down to the posted ramp speed or to a safe speed for the curve and conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:Only a suggested driving speed.,b:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,c:The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket in all circumstances.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions. You must reduce your speed below the limit when conditions are less than ideal, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or road work, to drive at a safe and reasonable speed.

question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Hide defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.,b:Assume it's the same as your car and go immediately.,c:Familiarize yourself with controls like turn signals
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to locate and test the turn signals, headlights, wipers, hazard lights, and mirrors. Adjust the seat and mirrors so you can see properly, and make sure there are no obvious safety defects. Being familiar with the controls helps you react quickly and safely in traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection, what should drivers follow?
options: a:The traffic light's instructions.,b:The officer's directions instead of the traffic signal.,c:Sound their horn to get attention.
note: When a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions override traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s directions even if the traffic signal shows a different indication, because they are managing traffic for safety or special conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally pass on the right when:
options: a:On a narrow bridge.,b:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,c:If the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
note: You may pass on the right only when it is legal and safe, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a clearly marked lane on the right for through traffic. You must stay on the paved roadway and never drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass, because that is unsafe and usually illegal.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Assume the flagger is not authorized to direct traffic.,b:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,c:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.
note: Flaggers are authorized to control traffic in work zones to protect workers and drivers. You must obey their signals and instructions, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Their directions may temporarily override normal signs or signals to keep the work zone safe.

question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
note: When rain begins, oil and dirt on the road mix with water and make the surface especially slippery. You should slow down, increase your following distance, and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. Driving faster or at the maximum speed limit in rain increases your risk of skidding or hydroplaning.

question: 'Highway hypnosis' can result from:
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods without scanning.
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods without actively scanning mirrors, signs, and surroundings. Your mind can drift even though your eyes are open, reducing awareness and reaction time. To prevent it, move your eyes regularly, check mirrors, vary your focus, and take regular breaks.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Look both ways and be prepared to yield before entering the intersection.,b:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.,c:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
note: A red and white triangle sign means YIELD. You must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and be ready to stop. Yield the right‑of‑way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection; proceed only when it is safe.

question: Larger vehicles compared with passenger cars have:
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have bigger blind spots than passenger cars, especially along the sides and directly behind them. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you. Avoid lingering in these blind areas and pass large vehicles quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield.,b:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals, even if no marked crosswalk exists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you drive when passing through school zones?
options: a:Observe the posted speed limits and be prepared for increased enforcement.,b:Always travel no faster than 10 mph.,c:Expect students to yield to vehicles rather than you yielding to them.
note: In school zones, you must obey the posted school speed limit and be especially alert for children who may enter the road unexpectedly. Slow down during posted school hours or when lights are flashing, watch for crossing guards, and be ready to stop at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection with heavy oncoming traffic but the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection to wait for a safe gap, or if you cannot turn safely, wait and use the next intersection.,b:Wait in the center of the intersection until traffic clears, even if the light turns red.,c:Turn immediately and force your turn.
note: With a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you may carefully move into the intersection and wait with your wheels straight until there is a safe gap or the light turns yellow/red and oncoming traffic stops. If you cannot turn safely, you may choose to wait and use the next intersection instead of entering and blocking traffic.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Turn on your windshield wipers.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Turn on headlights first.
note: When visibility is reduced by fog, heavy rain, snow, or darkness, the most important first response is to reduce your speed. Slowing down gives you more time to see hazards and react safely. You should also turn on your headlights and use wipers as needed, but matching your speed to what you can see is the primary safety step.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions.,b:It keeps traffic flowing faster.,c:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
note: A space cushion is the open space you keep in front of, behind, and to the sides of your vehicle. This space gives you time and room to react if another driver brakes suddenly, changes lanes, or makes a mistake. The more space you have, the more options you have to slow, stop, or steer around a hazard.

question: What is an effective way to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Only drive on side streets to avoid traffic.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your vehicle.,c:Communicate your intentions to other road users (such as using turn signals, brake lights, and the horn when necessary).
note: Crashes are less likely when other road users can predict what you are going to do. Use your turn signals before turning or changing lanes, tap your brake pedal early to show you are slowing, and use your horn only when necessary to alert others. Clear communication helps drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians adjust and avoid conflicts.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,c:Stop, then proceed when clear even if the red arrow is displayed.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped in the direction of the arrow until a green arrow or green light allows you to proceed. You may not turn in the direction of a red arrow unless a sign specifically allows turns on red at that location and you have come to a complete stop and yielded as required by local law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a railroad crossing without signals, you should:
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.
note: Many railroad crossings do not have lights or gates. When you approach a crossing without signals, you must slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching. Only stop every time if a sign or law requires it (such as for certain buses or trucks).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, you should indicate turns by using:
options: a:Your headlights,b:Your horn,c:Hand signals
note: If your turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show when you intend to turn or change lanes. Extend your left arm straight out for a left turn, bend your left arm up for a right turn, and bend it down for slowing or stopping so other drivers can anticipate your actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection but opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.,b:Accelerate quickly once the first lane is clear.,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.
note: At a multilane intersection, do not start your left turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists. Never rely on another driver waving you through, and do not accelerate blindly once only the first lane looks clear.

question: How is drinking alcohol and then driving classified?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving after drinking is a serious traffic safety problem because alcohol reduces judgment, coordination, and reaction time. Even a small amount can affect your ability to drive safely and greatly increases your risk of a crash.

question: When driving in fog, you should use:
options: a:Your high beams.,b:Your parking lights.,c:Your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights so the light aims down at the road and does not reflect back at you. High beams create glare in fog, rain, or snow and make it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe driving.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and immediately turn off the ignition.,b:Work harder to steer,c:Honk and keep driving normally until the car stops.
note: If power steering fails, the car can still be steered, but it will take much more physical effort. Keep a firm grip on the wheel, slow down, signal, and carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Do not turn off the ignition while moving, because that can lock the steering and disable power brakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn on multilane one-way streets or highways?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The middle of the intersection.,c:The left lane.
note: On a one‑way street with multiple lanes, you must begin a left turn from the leftmost lane that is properly marked and legal for turning. Starting from the far left helps you turn into the correct lane and avoids conflicts with traffic going straight or turning from other lanes.

question: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Drive to the right and stop immediately in all cases.,b:Stay in your lane and continue at speed.,c:Change lanes away and slow down if possible; if not safe to change lanes, slow down and proceed with caution
note: If safe, move over; otherwise slow down below the speed limit and pass with caution, giving the stopped vehicle more space.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, which lights should you use?
options: a:No lights unless it rains.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Headlights (low beam).
note: At dusk, dawn, and on overcast days, visibility is reduced, so you should turn on your low‑beam headlights. Low beams make your vehicle easier to see without creating glare for other drivers. Parking lights alone are not enough and are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: How should drivers adjust following distance in bad weather?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Maintain the same distance as in good weather.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or other bad weather, roads are more slippery and it takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: If you are involved in a serious vehicle crash, what is your first required action?
options: a:Drive away to report it later.,b:Just call your insurance company without stopping.,c:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop your vehicle at or near the scene. After stopping, move to a safe location if possible, check for injuries, and report the crash to law enforcement when required. Leaving without stopping is illegal in all states.

question: How does alcohol affect someone who drives after drinking?
options: a:They become better drivers because they are more careful.,b:They do not have sufficient control over their body,c:They are always aware of risks they are taking.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, affects coordination, and impairs judgment and vision. A driver who has been drinking does not have full control over their body or decisions, which makes driving unsafe even at low alcohol levels.

question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:In the opposite direction of the skid.
note: When your car begins to skid, you should steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This helps you regain control and straighten the vehicle. Overcorrecting or steering the opposite way can make the skid worse.

question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey the instruction shown?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do under the law, such as speed limits, stop, yield, and no-turn signs. You are legally required to obey them, and violations can result in tickets or other penalties.

question: Which action best describes a defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times.,b:Anticipates the actions of other drivers and watches for hazards.,c:Travels at a constant speed regardless of conditions.
note: A defensive driver stays alert, scans the road, and anticipates what other drivers, pedestrians, or cyclists might do. They adjust speed and position to avoid hazards instead of just maintaining a fixed speed or driving slowly without awareness.

question: How does cell phone use while driving affect safety?
options: a:It distracts drivers and can cause crashes.,b:It is not a problem in Idaho.,c:It is uncommon.
note: Using a cell phone while driving takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, and your mind off driving. This distraction greatly increases your chance of a crash. Many states, including Idaho, restrict or ban texting while driving and often require hands‑free use only.

question: Which of these does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,b:The time of day.,c:Your own reaction time.
note: Stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It depends on how quickly you see and react, your speed, your vehicle’s weight, and the condition of your brakes, tires, and the road surface. The time of day by itself does not change the physical stopping distance.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the correct response?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.,b:Overcorrect with quick steering movements.,c:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is usually the same direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding. This helps the tires regain traction and lets you straighten the vehicle smoothly without overcorrecting.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Signal and turn immediately without checking behind.,b:Rely solely on side mirrors for clearance.,c:Check mirrors and look over your left shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Signal in advance, make sure the lane is clear, and then move over smoothly. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles in your blind spots.

question: If you are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, you must:
options: a:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Drive with your flashers turned on.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as you safely can to the edge of the roadway and stopping until it has passed. On a one‑way street, pull to the nearest side (right or left) so the emergency vehicle has a clear path.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color and must be obeyed?
options: a:Blue,b:Green,c:White
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do (such as speed limits, no parking, or turn restrictions). In the U.S., these are typically white with black or red symbols or lettering, and they are legally enforceable, so you must obey them.

question: A single dashed white line between lanes indicates:
options: a:Drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed (broken) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and yielding as needed.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Black lines.,b:White lines.,c:Yellow lines.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction, while yellow centerlines warn you that oncoming traffic is using the other side of the line.

question: When you drive through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:They may run out in front of you without looking.,b:They will stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
note: Children near the road can be unpredictable and may suddenly run into the street without looking. When driving where children are playing, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time:
options: a:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals controlling the intersection.

question: The best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning is to:
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.,c:Watch out for standing water or puddles.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The most effective way to prevent this is to slow down when the road is wet or slushy, especially at higher speeds. Good tires and watching for standing water also help, but reducing speed is the single best way to lower the risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin to slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road, begin slowing well before the exit.,b:Only when you see a toll booth.,c:After you have moved fully into the exit (deceleration) lane.
note: On highways, you should maintain the normal traffic speed on the main roadway and not slow down until after you have entered the exit (deceleration) lane. Once fully in the exit lane, then reduce speed to the posted exit or ramp speed. Slowing on the main road can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Honk immediately before changing lanes.,b:Adjust rearview mirrors every few minutes instead of checking blind spots.,c:Quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, always quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot. Use your mirrors first, then check over your shoulder; do not rely only on mirrors or on honking.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Motion to the emergency vehicle to pass on the left.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle passes.,c:Slow down and continue at a reduced speed.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear, predictable path.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Drive around a lowered gate.,b:Speed up to cross before gates lower.,c:Look and listen for trains
note: Railroad crossings require extra caution because trains cannot stop quickly. As you approach tracks, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is coming, and never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train through the crossing.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:A regulation you must obey.,b:A direction to the nearest city.,c:A warning about existing or possible hazards ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert you to existing or possible hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or road work, so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: At an uncontrolled railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Be prepared to yield to any oncoming train before crossing.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Cross the tracks immediately as quickly as possible.
note: At an uncontrolled railroad crossing, you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Yield the right-of-way to any train; never cross unless you are sure no train is coming and there is enough room to clear all the tracks completely.

question: What steps should you take to cross railroad tracks safely?
options: a:Listen and look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe.,b:Cross quickly when you hear a train in the distance.,c:Only look both ways when the red light is flashing.
note: To cross railroad tracks safely, slow down, look and listen in both directions, and make sure there is enough space to drive completely across without stopping on the tracks. Only proceed when you are certain no train is coming and the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed under ideal conditions.,b:Potential driving speeds only.,c:The speed for heavy traffic only.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must reduce your speed when roads are wet, visibility is poor, traffic is heavy, or any condition makes driving at the posted limit unsafe.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you watch for before proceeding?
options: a:Whether the children wave at you.,b:Only the bus driver's signal.,c:Children walking along the side of the road.
note: After stopping for a school bus, be alert for children walking along the road, crossing in front of the bus, or running out from between vehicles. Do not proceed until the bus signals are off and you are sure all children are safely out of the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your car end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street (closest to the lane you left).,b:In the right lane.,c:In the center of the street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the lane closest to you—the left lane of the one-way street. This keeps traffic organized and prevents you from cutting across lanes where other vehicles may be traveling.

question: If you're upset or angry after an incident at work, what is the safest thing to do before driving home?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down and collect yourself before driving.,b:Play loud music to drown out your thoughts.,c:Drive fast to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions like anger or frustration can distract you and slow your reaction time. The safest choice is to pause, calm down, and regain your focus before driving so you can pay full attention to the road.

question: What does a single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Opposing traffic; passing is prohibited.,b:Opposing traffic; passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes moving in same direction only.
note: A single broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing in either direction when it is safe and legal. You must still check for oncoming traffic and ensure you have enough space and time to pass.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.,b:Slow down and regain control before gently steering back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Stop quickly in the traffic lane.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm and do not jerk the steering wheel. Ease off the accelerator, slow down gradually, and keep your wheels parallel to the road. When your speed is under control and it is safe, gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: What do downward-facing triangular traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Construction work is present.,b:School zones are ahead.,c:Drivers must yield.
note: A downward-facing (inverted) triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. It tells drivers to slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians before entering or crossing the roadway.

question: Does drinking coffee reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:It cancels the alcohol's effects.,b:It has no effect on BAC.,c:It decreases BAC.
note: Coffee may make you more alert but does not lower BAC or sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when:
options: a:Only when the center line on your side is broken and the road ahead is clear.,b:When you have enough clear distance ahead and passing is not prohibited by signs or road markings.,c:Never on hills, curves, or by using the shoulder of the road.
note: You may only pass another vehicle where it is legal and safe, typically when you have a broken (dashed) center line on your side and enough clear distance ahead. Passing on hills, curves, or on the shoulder is dangerous and illegal in standard U.S. rules because you cannot see far enough ahead or the shoulder is not a travel lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over one lane if it is safe and clear.,b:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.,c:Always remain at your present speed.
note: A merging traffic sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane. You should adjust your speed and, if it is safe and legal, move over a lane to create space. This helps traffic merge smoothly and reduces the risk of sudden braking or collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required when you encounter a flashing red light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and continue only if the intersection is clear.,b:Proceed only when a green light appears.,c:Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe and after yielding as needed.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear.

question: What lane width are motorcycles entitled to?
options: a:Half the width of a regular lane.,b:Only the bicycle lane.,c:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Other drivers should not crowd a motorcycle or share the same lane side‑by‑side with it, because motorcycles need space to maneuver and maintain a safety buffer.

question: Remember to signal when you:
options: a:Are changing lanes.,b:Pull into traffic from a parking area or alley.,c:Pull into or out of a parking space.,d:All of the above.
note: You should always signal before changing lanes, pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley, and when pulling into or out of a parking space. Signaling lets other drivers and pedestrians know what you intend to do so they can adjust safely and avoid collisions.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It decreases your chances of an accident.,b:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.,c:It can reduce your ability to concentrate on driving.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your focus, and slow your reactions, all of which reduce your ability to concentrate on driving. When you are upset or stressed, it is safer to calm down before driving or allow extra time and space on the road.

question: Orange-colored road signs typically indicate:
options: a:Work zone signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:School zone signs.
note: Orange signs are used for temporary traffic control in work and construction zones. They warn you about road work, lane closures, workers on or near the roadway, and changes in normal traffic patterns so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do to warn others and ensure safety?
options: a:Sound your horn at passing motorists for help.,b:Use your four-way flashers,c:Stay in the middle of the road and wave cars around you.
note: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, signal and carefully move as far off the roadway as possible, then turn on your four-way (hazard) flashers. Hazard lights and, if safe, raising your hood make your vehicle more visible so other drivers can see that you are stopped and avoid you.

question: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Only if it approaches from the opposite direction.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Whenever it is using lights or sirens
note: When an emergency vehicle is using its lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement. This applies whether the vehicle is coming from ahead, behind, or from a side street.

question: What does the term \No zone\" refer to?"
options: a:A designated no-passing zone on the roadway.,b:A one-way traffic area.,c:The large blind spot areas around trucks and other large vehicles.
note: “No zone” refers to the large blind spots around trucks and other large vehicles where the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision. Avoid lingering alongside or close behind large trucks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get through the intersection first.,b:Force the other vehicle to stop.,c:Yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), the general right‑of‑way rule is to yield to the vehicle on your right when you arrive at the same time. Slowing or stopping to let the vehicle on your right go first helps prevent confusion and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:When approaching a stopped school bus that is loading or unloading passengers with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended.,b:On hills or curves where vision is restricted.,c:Within about 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, or bridge where passing is prohibited by law.
note: Passing is prohibited in several high‑risk locations, including on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, within about 100 feet of intersections, railroad crossings, or bridges, and when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must never pass a stopped school bus from either direction on an undivided roadway while its red lights are flashing.

question: When driving in rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder for you to see and for others to see you. Low beams provide better visibility and reduce glare in these conditions.

question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which device?
options: a:CD player.,b:Radio.,c:Cell phone.
note: Using a cell phone while driving greatly increases crash risk because it takes your eyes, mind, and often a hand away from driving. This is true for both handheld and hands‑free use. While radios or CD players can distract you, cell phones involve more complex attention and are consistently linked to higher crash rates.

question: When you see other drivers acting angrily, you should:
options: a:Distance yourself from the situation.,b:Don't react with hand gestures.,c:Don’t make eye contact.
note: When you encounter an angry or aggressive driver, your goal is to avoid escalation and create space. Do not respond with gestures or eye contact, and safely increase the distance between your vehicle and theirs. Putting space between you and the aggressive driver is the most important safety step.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after vehicles ahead pass, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping again.,b:Slowly roll past the stop sign.,c:Come to a complete stop at the stop sign before proceeding.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must come to a complete stop at the proper stopping point, even if vehicles ahead have already stopped and gone. You must stop fully, check for traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:
options: a:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, drivers proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with double solid yellow center lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:You may cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:You may never cross them under any circumstances.,c:You may cross to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle. You may cross them only when making a left turn into or from an alley, private road, driveway, or similar location, and only when it is safe.

question: You must try to notify the owner of a vehicle if:
options: a:You hit their vehicle while it is unattended.,b:You don't like a bumper sticker displayed on their vehicle.,c:That they are breaking the law while talking on their cell phone while driving.
note: If you hit and damage an unattended vehicle, you are legally required to make a reasonable effort to find the owner. If you cannot locate them, you must leave a note with your name, address, and contact information, along with a brief description of the collision.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what should you ensure about seat belts?
options: a:That only child passengers are buckled.,b:That you and all passengers have fastened their seat belts.,c:That only adult passengers are buckled.
note: Before starting the vehicle, make sure you and every passenger are wearing a seat belt. The driver is responsible for ensuring that all occupants are properly restrained, especially children, before turning on the ignition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you:
options: a:Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.,b:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Are able to clearly see the road ahead.
note: You may only pass on a two-way, two-lane road when you can safely move back into your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. You must be able to see clearly ahead, judge that there is enough space and time to pass, and ensure your vehicle can complete the maneuver without forcing oncoming traffic or the vehicle you are passing to brake or swerve.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:Human error,c:New drivers
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, following too closely, speeding, or failing to yield. Weather and road conditions can contribute, but driver decisions and mistakes are the primary cause of most collisions.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, control the steering, and carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Brake hard and sharply turn back onto the pavement.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder and wait.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Slow down gradually, then when traffic and road conditions allow, gently steer back onto the pavement. Avoid hard braking or jerking the wheel, which can cause you to lose control.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway after a stop, what should you do?
options: a:Honking to let them know you are there.,b:Move to the left lane without slowing.,c:Yield to the transit vehicle to allow safe reentry.
