note: When a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the roadway after a stop, you must yield and allow it to merge safely. Be prepared to slow down, change lanes if safe, or stop if necessary so the bus can rejoin traffic without creating a hazard.

question: In which situation is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:To signal a pedestrian to hurry across.,b:To warn others if they may not see you or if a collision seems likely.,c:To celebrate passing another car.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of possible danger, such as when another road user may not see you or when a collision could occur. Do not use the horn to hurry pedestrians or to celebrate or express frustration.

question: What is the only reliable way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.,c:Exercise.
note: Only time reduces BAC. Coffee, exercise, and fresh air do not speed up the elimination of alcohol from the body.

question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, what must drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the light turns green or you are otherwise allowed to proceed (such as a permitted turn on red after stopping and yielding).,b:Continue driving if there is no cross traffic.,c:Slow down but roll through the intersection.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or limit line and remain stopped until the light turns green or you are otherwise allowed to proceed, such as making a permitted right turn on red after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

question: As a pedestrian, which behavior is safest?
options: a:Enter a crosswalk only when it is safe and you have checked for approaching traffic.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles, even if they cannot stop in time.,c:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are so close that they may not be able to stop safely.
note: Pedestrians generally have the right-of-way in crosswalks, but safety comes first. Never step into the street or a crosswalk when vehicles are so close that they cannot stop safely, even if you technically have the right-of-way.

question: Roads can become very slick under which conditions?
options: a:When the temperature is below freezing,b:When it has just started raining,c:Both of the above
note: Roads are especially slick just after rain begins, when oil and residue mix with water, and when temperatures are below freezing, allowing water to turn to ice. In both situations, you should slow down and increase following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers do when approaching a steady green traffic light?
options: a:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,b:Continue if the intersection is clear,c:Treat it like a four-way stop.
note: A steady green light means you may continue straight or turn if it is safe, but you must still yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and to any vehicles already in the intersection. Do not enter the intersection if it cannot be cleared safely.

question: If another driver is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up as they are passing you.,b:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,c:Stare at the driver as they pass.
note: When another driver is aggressive, focus on staying safe and avoiding conflict. Safely move out of their way, keep a generous following distance, and avoid eye contact or gestures that could escalate the situation.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your front wheels:
options: a:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,b:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward the curb and help stop the car.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow next to your lane and a broken yellow next to oncoming traffic, you may pass:
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear.
note: Yellow centerlines show where passing is allowed. If the solid yellow line is next to your lane and the broken yellow is on the other side, you may not pass. Only the side with the broken yellow line is allowed to pass when traffic is clear and it is safe.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream, what happens to your driving skills?
options: a:You become less confident and more cautious.,b:Your body metabolizes alcohol faster to offset impairment.,c:Your reaction time slows and you make more errors.
note: As alcohol builds up in your system, your reaction time slows, your judgment and coordination worsen, and you are more likely to make driving errors. You may feel more confident, but your actual driving ability is reduced.

question: Which of these actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Driving faster than the posted limit.,b:Using improper signals to hurry traffic.,c:Allowing extra travel time.
note: Allowing extra travel time reduces stress and the urge to rush, which helps prevent aggressive driving and road rage. Planning ahead, obeying speed limits, and signaling properly all contribute to calmer, safer interactions with other road users.

question: Which combination of actions helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure tires have good tread depth and are properly inflated.,b:Ensure tires are underinflated to increase contact area.,c:None of the above.
note: Good tread, correct tire pressure, and reducing speed in wet conditions all reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Night drives,b:High speeds,c:Slow speeds
note: Higher speeds mean it takes much longer to stop and crashes are far more severe because impact forces increase rapidly with speed. Slower speeds give you more time and distance to react and reduce the seriousness of any collision.

question: If you are taking an over-the-counter medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drink alcohol instead to counteract the medicine.,b:Assume it is safe if it was not prescribed to you.,c:Read the label for warnings about operating a vehicle.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read the label for warnings about driving or operating machinery, and ask a pharmacist or doctor if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive after taking the medication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After stopping at a stop sign, what is the recommended scanning sequence?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again before proceeding.,b:Look right first, then left, then right again.,c:Only check your rearview mirror.
note: After stopping at a stop sign, look left first because traffic from the left is usually closer and reaches you first. Then look right for approaching vehicles or pedestrians, and look left again to be sure it is still clear before you proceed.

question: Turning your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,b:A good driving habit.,c:A bad driving habit.
note: Turning your head to quickly check your blind spot before changing lanes is a key part of safe lane changing. Mirrors do not show everything; a shoulder check helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be alongside your car but outside your mirror view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Ignore it and proceed as usual.,c:Slow down and proceed with care after checking for hazards.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield or stop if there is cross traffic, pedestrians, or any other hazard in the intersection.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When exiting an expressway.,b:When following a motorcycle.,c:When following a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,d:All of the above.
note: You should increase your following distance in several situations, including when following a large vehicle that blocks your view, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, in bad weather, or when you need extra time to react. More space gives you a better view of the road ahead and more time to stop safely.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, what is the best practice?
options: a:Only have to know generally where your destination is.,b:Plan your trip in advance.,c:Should depend on road signs to find your way.
note: When driving to an unfamiliar area, plan your route before you start driving. Knowing your turns, exits, and alternatives ahead of time reduces last‑second lane changes, sudden stops, and distractions from trying to navigate while driving.

question: Which of the following is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Airbags are always safe for infants.,b:Children 12 and under must always ride in the front seat.,c:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger airbag.
note: Infants and small children should ride in proper child restraints in the back seat. A rear‑facing infant seat must never be placed in front of an active passenger airbag, because the airbag can seriously injure or kill the child. Children 12 and under are safest properly restrained in the rear seat, but some state laws focus on specific ages, sizes, and restraint types rather than a blanket rule for all under 13.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes you should:
options: a:Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.,b:Using the inside rearview mirror.,c:Using the outside rearview mirror.,d:By briefly turning your head and looking over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change.
note: To check blind spots when changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change. Mirrors alone cannot show blind spots, so use both your mirrors and a quick shoulder check before moving into another lane.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with drugs?
options: a:It decreases both effects.,b:It cures the illness.,c:The effects of both may increase
note: Mixing alcohol with many prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal drugs can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. This makes driving far more dangerous and increases the risk of a crash.

question: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and/or flashing lights?
options: a:Turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers and continue at the same speed.,b:Pull to the right and slow down but keep moving.,c:Pull to the right and stop immediately.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and/or flashing lights on, you must pull as close as safely possible to the right side of the road and stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:The right lane.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Either lane.
note: When turning left onto a one‑way street, you should turn into the lane closest to the lane you are coming from, usually the left lane of the one‑way street. Turning into the nearest appropriate lane helps keep traffic organized and prevents conflicts with other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is the meaning of this hand signal?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver intends to stop.,c:The driver intends to turn right.
note: Hand signals are used if your turn signals are not working: left arm straight out means a left turn, left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn, and left arm bent downward means slowing or stopping. A left arm extended upward therefore indicates a right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you generally do?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp then enter slowly.,b:Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.,c:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge into a gap.
note: When entering a highway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed so it closely matches the flow of traffic. Signal early, check mirrors and blind spot, and merge into a safe gap without forcing other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly.

question: Which of the following will limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory?
options: a:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can.,b:Alcohol does not affect those abilities.,c:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can slow your reactions and affect concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. You can be unsafe to drive even if you are below the legal limit, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking at all.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what is the first step?
options: a:Firmly apply the brakes.,b:Apply the parking brake.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On a slippery road, sudden braking can cause skids. First, gently ease your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle slows down gradually. If you need to slow more, apply the brakes smoothly and gently to maintain traction and control.

question: If you have been drinking socially, what practice helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Take a cold shower before driving.,c:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: The only safe choice after drinking is not to drive. Arrange a ride with a sober friend, use a taxi or rideshare, or stay where you are. Coffee, cold showers, or other tricks do not lower your blood alcohol level or make you safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Honk your horn at least three times.
note: Before passing, you must make sure it is safe and legal. Check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, signal, and ensure there is enough clear space ahead. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is plenty of space; you do not need to honk repeatedly or cut back in closely.

question: What risks do worn or bald tires present?
options: a:They improve fuel economy.,b:They reduce the risk of hydroplaning.,c:They can increase your stopping distance and make turning more difficult.
note: Worn or bald tires have much less traction, especially on wet roads. With less grip, your vehicle needs more distance to stop and is more likely to slide in turns, making steering and control harder. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road.

question: When are you not required to stop for a stopped school bus?
options: a:When the bus is unloading on your same side.,b:When traveling in the opposite direction on a roadway with four or more lanes.,c:When driving on a two-lane road in the opposite direction.
note: On divided or multi-lane roads with at least two lanes in each direction, drivers traveling in the opposite direction of a stopped school bus are generally not required to stop, as long as there is a physical or painted median separating directions. You must always stop when you are traveling in the same direction as the bus or on a simple two-lane road with no median, because children may cross the roadway.

question: At night, which road user is typically the hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs,b:Other motorists,c:Pedestrians
note: At night, pedestrians are often the hardest to see because they are small, may wear dark clothing, and usually do not have lights or reflectors. Headlights and streetlights make vehicles and signs more visible, but people on foot can blend into the background, so you must scan carefully, especially near crosswalks and along the road edge.

question: When roads are slippery, what should you do to reduce crash risk?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive the same as on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes regardless of conditions.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less grip, so it takes longer to stop and easier to skid. Increasing your following distance gives you more time and space to brake gently and avoid sudden steering or braking that could cause a loss of control.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Drive faster than the train.,c:Stop if a train is nearby.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign tells you tracks are ahead. You should slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or signals are activated. Never try to go around lowered gates or race a train; trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right-of-way.

question: Look over your shoulder to check blind spots when:
options: a:Turning left or right.,b:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Changing lanes.,d:All of the above.
note: You must check your blind spots by quickly looking over your shoulder whenever you change lanes, turn, or move toward or away from the curb. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in your blind spots, so a head check is needed before any lateral movement of your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct behavior for a vehicle entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Assume they have the right-of-way.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: When entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, you must adjust your speed to match traffic and yield to vehicles already on the highway. Merge only when there is a safe gap; you do not have the right-of-way over through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what is required of you?
options: a:Stop only if needed to avoid interfering with traffic or pedestrians.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or on the roadway you are entering. You only need to stop if traffic or pedestrians are close enough to make it unsafe to proceed without stopping.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels.,c:Directly into the lights.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane markings as a guide while still checking the road ahead frequently.

question: What types of drugs can impair your driving?
options: a:Only allergy medicine.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs
note: Many drugs can impair driving, including prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, and illegal drugs. Some can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, slower reaction time, or poor judgment, so always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: Before making a left turn, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Wait until there is a safe gap in traffic and the crosswalk is clear, then turn into the correct lane without swinging wide or sounding your horn unnecessarily.

question: The safest way to drive through a curve is to:
options: a:Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.,b:Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.,c:Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
note: For safe control in a curve, slow down before you enter, then gently accelerate as you pass the midpoint and exit. Braking hard in the curve can cause skidding, and entering too fast reduces your ability to stay in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach, you should:
options: a:Proceed through the intersection; a yellow light is only a caution sign.,b:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,c:Always stop immediately, even if you must brake suddenly in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop without hard braking or risking a rear‑end collision, continue through the intersection with caution.

question: Which factors influence blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Only how much you weigh.,b:Only the type of alcoholic beverage.,c:Amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it is consumed, body weight, and food intake.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is mainly affected by how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and how much food is in your stomach. Food can slow the rate alcohol enters your bloodstream but does not prevent impairment. The type of drink matters only because different drinks contain different amounts of alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are drivers required to stop their vehicle?
options: a:At stop signs, steady red lights, flashing red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:Only when a red light is flashing.
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at steady red lights, at flashing red lights, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop. Stopping allows you to yield the right‑of‑way when required and prevents entering intersections or crossings when it is unsafe.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The increased possibility of encountering pedestrians.,b:The reduced school speed limit has ended.,c:That the speed limit is 20 mph.
note: An 'End school zone' sign tells you that the special reduced school speed limit is over. After passing this sign, you follow the regular posted speed limit for that area, unless another sign indicates a different limit.

question: What do regulatory traffic signs communicate?
options: a:They indicate what drivers must or must not do.,b:They warn of hazardous conditions.,c:They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do (such as obey a speed limit) or must not do (such as no U-turn). They communicate legal requirements, not just warnings or general information, and ignoring them can result in citations.

question: On slick roads, you should:
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly.,c:Accelerate quickly.
note: On slick or slippery roads, you should slow down and make all movements—steering, braking, and accelerating—more gently. Taking turns more slowly helps maintain traction and reduces the chance of skidding.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash indicate?
options: a:Drivers must come to a complete stop.,b:The specified action is prohibited.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash over a symbol means that the pictured action is not allowed. For example, a left-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no left turns at that location.

question: Pennant-shaped signs are used to indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs, placed on the left side of the road, mark the beginning of a no-passing zone. When you see this sign, you must not start to pass another vehicle in that area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by other traffic, you should:
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. If traffic ahead is stopped and you would be forced to stop in the intersection, you must wait behind the stop line or crosswalk until there is enough space to drive all the way through without blocking cross traffic.

question: When you first get into a car, what should you adjust first if needed?
options: a:Your seat so you can reach controls and see clearly.,b:Your seat belt.,c:Your rearview mirror.
note: Before driving, adjust your seat so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, adjust mirrors and then fasten and adjust your seat belt.

question: When backing up, what is the recommended way to check for hazards?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Open your door to check behind you.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.
note: When backing up, place your right arm over the back of the passenger seat, turn your head and shoulders, and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Mirrors and cameras can help, but you should not rely on them alone.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Pump your brakes rapidly before stopping.,b:Stop abruptly to warn drivers behind you.,c:Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas to slow, then brake smoothly when needed.
note: To reduce the risk of being hit from behind, look well ahead and slow down gradually by first easing off the accelerator, then braking smoothly. Avoid sudden, hard stops whenever possible so drivers behind you have time to see your brake lights and react.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady green.,b:Steady red.,c:Flashing yellow.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if you are too close to stop safely, proceed with caution before the light turns red.

question: Which rule applies to bicyclists in Idaho regarding stop signs?
options: a:Bicyclists must stay off sidewalks.,b:Bicyclists are not required to always come to a complete stop at stop signs but must yield to vehicles already at the intersection.,c:Bicyclists must always come to a full stop at stop signs.
note: In Idaho, bicyclists may treat a stop sign as a yield sign. They must slow, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way, and proceed only when it is safe. They are not always required to come to a complete stop if the intersection is clear and they can safely yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light corresponds with:
options: a:A solid green light.,b:A solid red light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe. It does not correspond to a solid green light, which means go if the intersection is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:You are on a two-lane,b:The vehicle you are overtaking is driving below the speed limit and you must use the shoulder of the road to pass.,c:You are on a multilane highway and the vehicle you are overtaking is driving below the speed limit.
note: Passing on the right is only allowed when it can be done safely within a marked lane and without leaving the main‑traveled portion of the roadway. Using the shoulder to pass is illegal, even if the vehicle ahead is going below the speed limit.

question: An inattentive driver is one who:
options: a:Only watches the vehicle ahead of them.,b:Maintains eye contact during conversation with a passenger.,c:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is mentally or visually distracted from the driving task, such as daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway. This reduces awareness of traffic conditions and greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving, you should:
options: a:Blow your horn.,b:Turn on your four-way flashers.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep calm, shift to neutral, and apply the brakes smoothly while you steer to a safe place off the road. Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers, and turn off the ignition only when you are safely off the roadway.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and creep across the tracks.,b:Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and look for a train.,c:Speed up and cross before the train arrives.
note: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you must stop and not proceed until the lights stop and it is clearly safe. Stopping at least 15 feet from the nearest rail gives space for the train and prevents you from being trapped on the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off to the right and let traffic pass when safe to do so.,b:Continue at the same slow speed regardless of backups.,c:Refuse to let following cars pass by blocking them.
note: If your slow driving is causing a line of vehicles to form behind you, you are impeding traffic. When it is safe, pull off to the right or into a turnout so faster traffic can pass, then re-enter when clear.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings must be obeyed.,b:Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are optional.,c:Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings apply only when other traffic is present.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that all drivers must obey. Ignoring them or treating them as suggestions is unsafe and against the law.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be harder to see and notice in traffic than other vehicles.,b:They always follow different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and less visible than cars and trucks, especially in blind spots, at night, or in heavy traffic. Because they are more vulnerable in a crash, drivers must scan carefully and give them extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper way to enter a freeway?
options: a:Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic, signal, and merge when safe.,b:Signal, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.,c:Enter slowly and expect freeway traffic to yield to you.
note: To enter a freeway safely, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed, signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge smoothly into a gap in traffic. You must yield to freeway traffic; do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed quickly because they have the right-of-way.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield to them.,c:Slow down gradually while checking mirrors and signal in advance.
note: Before turning left, you should signal well in advance, check your mirrors and blind spots, slow down smoothly, and be prepared to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Only complete the turn when the path is clear and safe.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the roadway?
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:Only on hills and curves.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks. You must stop with the front of your vehicle just before this line when required to stop by a sign, signal, or traffic officer.

question: About half of all motorcycle crashes involve what?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:Only minor injuries with no fatalities.,c:Another motor vehicle.
note: About half of all motorcycle crashes involve another motor vehicle, often because the driver did not see the motorcycle or misjudged its speed. Always check mirrors and blind spots carefully and look twice for motorcycles before turning or changing lanes.

question: What type of signs warn drivers about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs (typically yellow and diamond-shaped).
note: Warning signs are usually yellow and diamond-shaped and alert you to hazards such as curves, intersections, pedestrian areas, or changes in road conditions. Slow down and be prepared to adjust your driving when you see these signs.

question: Where should pedestrians yield to motor vehicles?
options: a:When the motor vehicle is a pickup truck.,b:When crossing at a marked crosswalk.,c:When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.
note: Pedestrians must yield to vehicles when crossing the road at places without a crosswalk or intersection, such as mid‑block. At marked or unmarked crosswalks at intersections, drivers are generally required to yield to pedestrians who are crossing legally.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the dividing line between lanes is which type?
options: a:Solid yellow line.,b:Broken white line.,c:Double solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so. Solid yellow lines and double solid yellow lines generally mean passing is not allowed.

question: On a road without sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.,b:On the same side and direction as traffic.,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and react if a driver drifts toward the edge of the road.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down continuously.,b:Lightly tap the brakes.,c:Firmly pump your brakes.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, use firm pumping of the brakes in an emergency stop. Press the brake firmly, then release slightly before the wheels lock, and repeat. This helps you slow quickly while still being able to steer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you pass another vehicle within an intersection in Idaho?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If a dashed and a solid yellow line are marked through the intersection.,c:If a dashed yellow pavement marking continues through the intersection.
note: In Idaho, you may pass in an intersection only if passing is otherwise legal and the dashed yellow centerline continues through the intersection. A solid yellow line at the intersection means passing is not allowed there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,c:Ask another driver for help through your window.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, continue to the next exit, leave the highway safely, and then return to the correct exit. Never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the highway.

question: If you must drive in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low-beam headlights.,b:Hazard lights only.,c:High-beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low‑beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare, improving your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the road.

question: What is the usual effect of being distracted while driving?
options: a:It makes drivers drive faster.,b:It always improves driver awareness.,c:It causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.
note: Distractions such as phones, passengers, or adjusting controls take your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving. This usually causes slower reaction times and delayed responses to hazards, increasing the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling your intentions before turning or changing lanes is:
options: a:Necessary only during the maneuver,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:A good driving habit and is required by law.
note: You must signal in advance (at least 100 feet where applicable) before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb so other road users can anticipate your actions.

question: What does a 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign mean when you encounter it?
options: a:The new 35 mph limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,b:You may stay at your current speed until you feel ready to slow down.,c:The new 35 mph speed limit starts at that sign.
note: A regulatory speed limit sign, such as one that reads “Reduced speed 35 mph,” means the posted speed limit is 35 mph beginning at that sign. You are expected to have already slowed so that you are at or below 35 mph as you reach the sign, not sometime later down the road.

question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You become more alert.
note: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows reflexes and reaction time, harms judgment of speed and distance, and reduces alertness. It does not make you more alert; believing that it does is dangerous and incorrect.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drive immediately because emotions won’t affect you.,b:Take time to calm down and focus before starting the engine.,c:Drive faster because you are more alert.
note: Strong emotions like anger, fear, or sadness can distract you, slow your reactions, and cause poor decisions. You should always take time to calm down and focus before starting the engine so you can give full attention to the road.

question: During a tire blowout, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Accelerate to maintain control then pull over.,b:Take your foot off the accelerator and slow down gradually.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately to stop quickly.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle slows down gradually. Do not slam on the brakes, because sudden braking can cause you to lose control. Steer straight, let the car slow, then gently brake and pull off the road when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to do what?
options: a:Yield to traffic only from the left.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Stop and treat the intersection like a stop sign
note: A flashing red light means you must make a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the speed limit illegal?
options: a:Only in rural areas.,b:When in heavy construction traffic.,c:When driving slowly disrupts the normal traffic flow.
note: It's unlawful to drive so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow; you may be cited for driving too slowly.

question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed management in curves?
options: a:Maintain posted speed and slow at the sharpest part.,b:Accelerate gently into the curve.,c:Slow down before you enter the curve.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve, not while you are already in it. Entering too fast can cause your vehicle to slide outward due to inertia and reduce your ability to steer safely through the curve.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance.,b:Approach all vehicles with caution.,c:Drive faster to get out of bad weather.
note: In sleet or snow, visibility and traction are reduced. Keep your windshield, windows, and mirrors clear so you can see, and increase your following distance because it takes much longer to stop on slippery roads. Never speed up to try to “outrun” bad weather.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what should you do first?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: A green light means you may go only after you first check the intersection and yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still clearing the intersection. Do not accelerate immediately without looking; the intersection must be clear and it must be safe before you proceed.

question: Which of the following is true about passing motorcycles?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:A motorcycle with two people on it is more balanced than a motorcycle with just one rider.,c:It is okay for drivers of other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like a car. When passing, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and pass as you would another vehicle, leaving plenty of space. Do not crowd the motorcycle or share the lane, and never follow a motorcycle too closely because they can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles.

question: What color background do guide/destination signs have?
options: a:Red.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.
note: Guide and destination signs that show routes, cities, and distances use a green background with white letters and symbols. These signs help you navigate to places and follow highway routes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must stop at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, you should:
options: a:Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersecting roadway.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:You are only required to slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection, at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. You should not pull into the cross street just to improve your view; stop first where you can see without entering the intersecting roadway, then move forward carefully if you need a better view.

question: Where is it important to slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, at intersections or railroad crossings, and when roads are slippery.,b:Only on steep hills.,c:Only when pedestrians are present.
note: You must reduce speed in situations where hazards are more likely: narrow or winding roads, intersections, railroad crossings, and when the road is wet or slippery. Slowing down gives you more time to react and helps prevent skids or loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Stop immediately only if there are vehicles to your left.,b:Proceed without stopping.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop; a red light will soon appear.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. Do not speed up to beat the red light.

question: Always use signals when:
options: a:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Changing lanes.,d:All of the above.
note: Turn signals must be used whenever you change direction or move your vehicle laterally: when changing lanes, turning, entering traffic from an alley or parking area, and when pulling into or out of a parking space. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your movements and helps prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right.,b:Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.,c:Maintain their speed and proceed.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must be prepared to yield the right‑of‑way. Slow down, look left‑right‑left, and yield to any traffic already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right. You do not always have to stop, but you must be ready to yield so you can avoid a collision.

question: You can avoid alcohol-related crash risk by:
options: a:Calling a taxi or arranging other transportation.,b:Simply saying, "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.,c:Deciding before you start drinking that you are not going to drive.,d:All of the above are ways to avoid alcohol‑related crash risk.
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to plan ahead: decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Arrange a designated driver, use a taxi or rideshare, or choose not to drink if you must drive. Once you have been drinking, your judgment is already impaired, so advance planning is critical.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and look for police cars first.,b:Maintain your normal speed without yielding.,c:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection before turning.
note: On a green light you may turn right, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in or entering the intersection. Do not simply maintain speed; slow as needed, check for pedestrians and oncoming traffic, and complete the turn only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a slow-moving heavy truck from behind on a hill, what should you expect?
options: a:You are always able and allowed to pass the truck safely.,b:The truck must move over for you.,c:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down on hills because of their weight and engine limits, so you should expect them to travel below the posted speed. Be patient, keep a safe following distance, and only pass if it is legal, you have enough clear sight distance, and you can complete the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best practice?
options: a:Proceed slowly and wait for a special opening.,b:Turn on your hazard lights until merged.,c:Accelerate on the ramp to match traffic speed and blend in safely.
note: Use the freeway entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of freeway traffic, then merge when there is a safe gap. Signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and remember that entering traffic must yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: Where should you try to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only on the left and right sides.,b:Only in back of your vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: A space cushion on all sides gives you time and room to react to sudden stops, lane changes, or hazards. Leave enough following distance in front, allow space behind when possible, and avoid driving right next to other vehicles so you have an escape path if something goes wrong.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:May no longer turn and must proceed straight.,b:May still turn.,c:Still have the right-of-way to turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn with the right‑of‑way. When it changes to a solid green light, you may still turn, but it becomes an unprotected turn. You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and only turn when there is a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger.,b:It is controlled by a stop sign.,c:Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a flagger directs you to stop, when there is a stop sign at the crossing, or when flashing red lights and/or gates indicate a train is coming. These controls mean a train may be approaching and you must stop and proceed only when it is safe and legal.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medication?
options: a:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.,b:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,c:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
note: Alcohol can dangerously interact with many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines. When combined, the effects of the alcohol, the medicine, or both can be multiplied, causing much greater drowsiness, slowed reaction time, and poor judgment than either would alone.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should:
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will move back and gently touch the curb, helping stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic.

question: What can occur when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be reduced.,b:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,c:Nothing will happen.
note: Mixing alcohol with another drug often increases the effects of both. This can greatly increase drowsiness, confusion, and slowed reactions, making driving far more dangerous than using either substance alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing not permitted?
options: a:On a hill or curve where you cannot see ahead.,b:When a school bus is stopped and its lights are flashing.,c:When approaching an intersection.
note: You may never pass a school bus that is stopped with its red lights flashing; traffic in both directions must stop (unless separated by a physical median where state law allows otherwise). Passing is also prohibited on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, at or near intersections, and anywhere signs or pavement markings indicate no passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:On a hill.,b:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because these areas must remain clear for pedestrians and cyclists. Parking on a hill is allowed if no signs prohibit it and you park properly with wheels turned correctly and within the required distance from the curb. Parking in a parking lot is allowed where spaces are designated and no signs restrict it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:
options: a:The presence of a stop sign.,b:The use of your turn signals.,c:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
note: To cross traffic safely, you must have a large enough gap based on how fast other vehicles are moving, how good your traction and visibility are, and how quickly you can accelerate. Wet or slippery roads, poor visibility, and heavy oncoming traffic all mean you need a larger gap before crossing or turning.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roads is true?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires are less effective at clearing water and hydroplaning risk increases.,b:Good tires eliminate any risk from water.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: On wet roads, the faster you drive, the harder it is for your tires to channel water away. This increases the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road. Good tires reduce but do not eliminate this risk, and deeper water is more dangerous, not less. Slow down and increase following distance in wet conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about passing is true?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,b:When passing another vehicle, it is not necessary to check your blind spot.,c:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.
note: Before passing another vehicle, you must signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you are moving. This over-the-shoulder check is critical because vehicles can be hidden where mirrors do not show them. Only move into the passing lane when it is clear and safe, and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which practice is especially important?
options: a:Make sure the lane is clear using your mirrors only before moving.,b:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,c:Signal your intentions in advance but rely only on your mirrors.
note: When changing lanes, you must always check your blind spot by quickly glancing over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Mirrors and turn signals are important, but they do not show vehicles in your blind spots. A quick over-the-shoulder check helps you avoid colliding with a vehicle that is beside you but not visible in your mirrors.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When you hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you, you must safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop, allowing it a clear path to pass. Use your mirrors, signal, and move smoothly; do not stop in an intersection.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle through.,c:Stop where you are and wait.
note: The correct response to an emergency vehicle with siren and/or flashing lights behind you is to pull over to the right side of the road and stop, when safe. Do not speed up or stop in the middle of the lane; instead, create a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Disregard the signal if there are other lanes available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Slow down but do not change lanes.,c:Move safely out of the emergency vehicle's path and stop until it has passed.
note: On any roadway, including a divided multilane highway, you must yield to approaching emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Safely move out of their path and stop until they have passed. Do not ignore them or just slow slightly; come to a stop where it is safe so they can get through quickly.

question: Which of the following is true about work zones?
options: a:They never require drivers to slow down or pay extra attention.,b:They may be stationary or involve moving operations and are marked with orange signs.,c:They are marked only by black and white signs.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (like a fixed construction area) or moving (such as striping or mowing operations). They are identified by orange signs and often cones or barrels. Drivers must slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and stay especially alert for workers and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When do you have the right-of-way for a left turn?
options: a:When a green arrow pointing left is showing.,b:When a solid green light is on.,c:When a flashing yellow appears.
note: A steady green left arrow means oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you are stopped, so you have the right-of-way to make a protected left turn. With a solid green light or flashing yellow arrow, you may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: When roads are slippery, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more quickly to get through the slippery area sooner.,b:Maintain the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads you must slow down and drive below the posted speed if needed. Reduced speed and a greater following distance give you more time and space to react and help prevent skids.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (driving with one hand and talking), you should:
options: a:Know that the driver in the vehicle ahead is reducing their safety margin by being an inattentive driver.,b:Give the vehicle extra space.,c:Avoid following the driver's example.
note: When another driver is distracted, you should increase the space around your vehicle. Giving them extra following distance reduces your risk if they brake suddenly, drift in their lane, or fail to notice hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Continue driving and use the next exit.,c:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop, back up, cut across traffic, or make a U‑turn on the interstate, as these maneuvers are extremely dangerous and usually illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving.,b:Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Accelerate to avoid a red light.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. Only continue through if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Be ready to stop.,b:Look for a train.,c:Slow down.
note: When approaching any railroad crossing, you should slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Trains cannot stop quickly, so you must always be ready to stop if a train is approaching or signals are active.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach, what is the best action?
options: a:Be prepared to stop safely; do not speed up to beat the red.,b:Speed up to make it through the intersection.,c:Brake sharply in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the intersection, rather than speeding up to beat the red or braking hard in the middle of the intersection.

question: When are road surfaces most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:The day after it rains.,b:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rainfall.
note: Roads are usually most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm because water lifts oil and other residues to the surface. After it has rained for a while, much of this buildup is washed away and traction generally improves.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching in your area, what is your duty?
options: a:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by safely moving out of its path—typically by pulling to the right and stopping when possible—so it can pass quickly and safely.

question: How should you treat a vehicle that has just parked at the side of the road when passing it?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to be safe.,b:Assume the driver may open a door and use extra caution.,c:Speed up to pass quickly.
note: When passing a parked vehicle, assume someone may open a door or pull out into traffic. Slow slightly if needed, leave extra space, and be prepared to react so you can avoid a sudden door opening or vehicle movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Assume the guard is mistaken.,b:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,c:Follow what surrounding traffic does regardless of the guard.
note: In a school zone, you must obey the crossing guard’s directions, even if they differ from traffic signals. Crossing guards help children cross safely, so follow their signals and drive with extra caution and reduced speed.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Flash your high beams at the driver.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
note: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and simply adjust your speed or position to maintain a safe following distance. Reacting aggressively can quickly escalate into road rage and greatly increase the risk of a collision.

question: If you hear a siren and cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.,b:Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.,c:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
note: When you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull as far to the right as possible and stop, then look and listen to locate the vehicle. Remain stopped until you are sure the emergency vehicle has passed or it is clear that it is not on your street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through a stop-sign-controlled intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing down and checking for traffic.,b:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it is safe.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection—typically at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic. Proceed only when you are sure it is safe and you have yielded to any vehicles or pedestrians with the right-of-way.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,b:It is more likely to be raining at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark.
note: Night driving is harder because you can see less: darkness reduces your overall visibility, depth perception, and contrast, making it harder to spot hazards. You should slow down and make sure you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.

question: What should you avoid doing on potentially slippery roads?
options: a:Keeping a large following distance.,b:Reducing your speed and driving carefully.,c:Using cruise control and making sudden speed or direction changes.
note: On slippery roads, sudden acceleration, braking, or steering can cause you to lose traction, and cruise control can prevent you from reacting quickly to changing conditions. Instead, reduce your speed, increase following distance, and make all changes in speed and direction gradually.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by whom?
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle at all times.,b:The driver only.,c:Passengers only on long drives.
note: All occupants should wear seat belts on every trip; unbelted passengers can become projectiles in a crash and injure others.

question: To prepare for any hazards ahead on the road, you should:
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,c:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors regularly. This helps you spot hazards early, such as slowing traffic, pedestrians, or vehicles entering from side streets, so you have time to react smoothly. Staring straight ahead narrows your field of vision and resting your foot on the brake can cause unnecessary braking and wear.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if its lights are flashing and it's stopped to load/unload children.,b:When it is parked on the shoulder empty.,c:Whenever you see a bus approaching regardless of lights.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and/or stop arm extended. This signals that children are getting on or off and may be crossing the road. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, then proceed with extra caution.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance and time to stop. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, give them extra space, and remember they also have larger blind spots and need more room to turn and maneuver.

question: When driving with other vehicles on the road, what is the safest general approach?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic while obeying the posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to avoid conflicts.,c:Drive significantly slower than everyone else.
note: The safest approach is to move with the general flow of traffic while staying at or below the posted speed limit. Driving much faster can lead to crashes and tickets, while driving much slower than surrounding traffic can cause others to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which sequence of actions should you take?
options: a:Signal only — mirrors are optional.,b:Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder before moving.,c:Check the blind spot only after beginning the lane change.
note: For a safe lane change, you must signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving into the new lane. Signaling alone is not enough, and you should always check the blind spot before you start moving over, not after.

question: When near a motorcycle, you must allow it to:
options: a:Use a full lane.,b:Use the shoulder while you share the lane.,c:Use only half a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane, just like any other motor vehicle. You must not crowd them, share their lane, or force them onto the shoulder. Always give motorcycles a full lane and extra following distance.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effects of alcohol.,b:The effects of amphetamines.,c:The effects of simple anger.
note: Fatigue slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and impairs judgment in ways very similar to alcohol. Being awake for long periods can affect driving ability about as much as having a moderate blood alcohol concentration, so you should never drive when you are very tired.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow displayed by a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Is never used as a traffic signal.,c:Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light (prepare to stop).
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending and the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so. It has the same meaning for that turn as a circular yellow light has for through traffic.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are a police officer.,b:They are likely blind.,c:They are deaf.
note: A white cane (with or without a red tip) or a guide dog identifies a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. You must use extra caution, slow down, and yield the right-of-way, stopping if necessary to allow them to cross safely.

question: Which recommendation does not help night driving safety?
options: a:Looking into oncoming headlights to adjust your vision.,b:Keep your windshield clean.,c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
note: At night you should never look directly into oncoming headlights because the glare can temporarily blind you and reduce your ability to see the road. Keeping your windshield clean reduces glare and improves visibility, and having a flashlight in the vehicle can help you see and stay safe if you must stop or deal with an emergency in the dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes or turning, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal your intention well in advance, even if no traffic is immediately visible.,b:Only signal when other vehicles are visible.,c:Signal only in daylight.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb, even if you do not immediately see other traffic. Signaling early gives other road users time to see your intentions and react safely, which helps prevent collisions.

question: What does a solid white line between lanes indicate on a multi-lane road?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A solid white line between lanes means traffic in those lanes is moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or sometimes prohibited. You should stay in your lane unless you must change and it is clearly safe and legal to do so.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:You must stop and back up immediately.,b:That it is summer.,c:Less-than-ideal driving conditions; exercise extra caution.
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work is taking place and normal conditions may be changed. You should slow down, be prepared for lane shifts, workers, equipment, and sudden stops, and drive with extra caution through the area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Idaho's GDL program, what passenger restrictions apply during the first six months of driving for a licensee under age 17?
options: a:No passengers under age 18 are permitted,b:No more than one passenger under age 17 is permitted (unless related by blood, marriage, or adoption),c:Only family members are permitted,d:No restrictions apply
note: In Idaho, drivers under age 17 are restricted to carrying no more than one passenger under age 17 during the first six months of licensure, unless the passenger is an immediate family member.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the nighttime driving restriction for an Idaho permit or license holder who is under age 16?
options: a:Cannot drive between 10:00 PM and 5:00 AM,b:Cannot drive between midnight and 5:00 AM,c:May only drive during daylight hours (unless accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older in the front seat),d:No nighttime driving restrictions apply
note: Under Idaho law, drivers under the age of 16 are restricted to driving during daylight hours only, unless they are accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old sitting in the passenger seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Idaho law, what is the minimum property damage threshold that requires you to immediately report a traffic crash to the police?
note: In Idaho, you must immediately report any traffic accident to the police or sheriff if it results in injury, death, or damage to property of any one person of $1,500 or more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the minimum auto liability insurance coverage limits required for all motor vehicles registered in Idaho?
note: Idaho law requires all drivers to maintain liability insurance coverage of at least 25/50/15: $25,000 for bodily injury per person, $50,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $15,000 for property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Idaho law, what is the special speed exception when passing another vehicle on a two-lane highway?
options: a:You may exceed the limit by up to 5 mph on any road,b:You may exceed the limit by up to 10 mph on any road,c:You may exceed the limit by up to 15 mph if the posted limit is 55 mph or greater,d:You are never permitted to exceed the speed limit when passing
note: In Idaho, when passing a slower vehicle on a two-lane highway with a posted speed limit of 55 mph or higher, you may exceed the posted speed limit by up to 15 mph to complete the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Idaho's point system, accumulating how many points within a 12-month period will result in a 30-day driver's license suspension?
options: a:8 to 11 points,b:12 to 17 points,c:18 to 23 points,d:24 or more points
note: In Idaho, accumulating 12 to 17 points on your driving record within a 12-month period results in a mandatory 30-day license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an Idaho teen under the age of 17 violates any GDL restriction or traffic law during the supervised instruction period, what happens to their permit?
options: a:They receive a warning letter,b:Their parents must pay a fine,c:The permit is canceled, and they must reapply and restart the 6-month supervised period,d:Their permit is suspended for 15 days
note: If an Idaho permit holder under 17 violates any GDL restrictions or is convicted of any traffic violation, the permit will be canceled, and they must reapply and restart the 6-month supervised driving requirement from the beginning.
